years.formatNotes: Inaugural CrossFit Games. No qualification process - anyone could register and compete. Three individual events over two days; the first event was kept secret and drawn at random on the morning of competition from a 'hopper' (a peanut roaster filled with colored balls), reflecting Greg Glassman's belief that the fittest athlete should be ready for any task. On-site scaling was permitted and scaled scores were ranked below Rx on the leaderboard. Overall placing was determined by points across the three events (archived leaderboard shows a 100-points-for-first style table: Fitzgerald won with 272, Gentry with 290); the exact 2007-era points table was never formally published. Individual champions each received 500 dollars. An affiliate team competition (won by CrossFit Santa Cruz) ran the same weekend but is not part of the individual record. Field counts are starters per the official leaderboard archive (44 men, 20 women): every listed athlete recorded a score in at least one event, so all 44 men and 20 women are counted as starters. Several athletes withdrew from individual events (e.g. three men, including Keegan Martin, show WD on the hopper workout but scored the CrossFit Total or trail run; five women show WD on one or two events), so per-event starter counts are lower than the overall field. Roughly 70 athletes attended in total with about 150 spectators.
years.yearSummary: The first CrossFit Games were a grassroots gathering on Dave Castro's family ranch in Aromas, California, with no qualifiers, roughly 70 athletes, and a 500 dollar prize per champion. Programming established themes that would define the sport: an unknown-and-unknowable element (the hopper-drawn row/pull-up/push-jerk triplet), a pure monostructural test (an approximately 5K trail run over the ranch's steep hills), and a pure strength test (the CrossFit Total of back squat, press, and deadlift maxes). James Fitzgerald (OPT) took the men's title on consistency - second in both day-one events - while Jolie Gentry won the hopper workout outright and finished second in the other two to dominate the women's field. Every movement contested was by definition a Games debut, and the hopper workout proved iconic enough to be recreated as the event '2007' at the 2013 Games.

events.name: Hopper-Style CrossFit WOD
events.description:
For time:
1,000-meter row (Concept-2)
Then, 5 rounds of:
25 pull-ups
7 push jerks (135 lb men / 85 lb women)

The workout was drawn at random on the morning of competition from a hopper (a peanut roaster filled with colored balls). On-site scaling was permitted: leaderboard scores show men scaling to 95 lb jerks and/or jumping pull-ups, and women to 65 lb.
events.notes: First event ever contested at a CrossFit Games. Women's load conflict: the archived official games.crossfit.com workout page and WODwell list 85 lb; the Wikipedia article says 95 lb - the official source (85 lb) is used here. No official time cap is documented; athletes who did not finish were recorded by round/rep progress (e.g. 'Rnd 5 25 Pullups') and the slowest recorded finish was exactly 20:00, suggesting a cutoff near 20 minutes, but this is unconfirmed. Brett Marshall (AFT) won the men's event using butterfly pull-ups; overall champion James Fitzgerald was second (13:39). The workout was recreated as event '2007' at the 2013 Games (there with a 15-minute cap).

events.name: Trail Run
events.description:
Trail run, approximately 5 kilometers (about 3 miles), for time.
Off-road course over the steep, hilly terrain of the Castro family ranch in Aromas. No added load. Contested in the afternoon of day one, after the hopper workout.
events.notes: Exact course length was never published; the official archived workout page lists it only as 'Trail run (approximately 5 k)'. Chris Spealler edged overall champion James Fitzgerald (20:45) by two seconds.

events.name: CrossFit Total
events.description:
CrossFit Total - sum of the heaviest successful single repetition in each of:
Back squat, 1-rep max
Shoulder press, 1-rep max
Deadlift, 1-rep max

Loads were athlete-selected maximal attempts (no prescribed weights). Per Wikipedia, athletes had up to 3 attempts at each lift, taken within 4-minute windows. Score is the combined total in pounds.
events.notes: First pure strength test at the Games, using Mark Rippetoe's CrossFit Total benchmark (CrossFit Journal, 2006). The 3-attempts-per-lift / 4-minute-window detail comes from Wikipedia and could not be verified against an official source. Loads array is empty because all weights were athlete-selected maxes. Olympic lifter Josh Everett was second among men (1133 lb); event winner Connor Banks finished 14th overall after placing 31st in both day-one events. Leaderboard spells the women's winner 'Nichole Dehart' (Wikipedia uses 'Nicole').

years.formatNotes: No qualification process: open registration, first-come first-served, capped at roughly 300 competitor slots (sold out, then briefly reopened for a limited number). Scoring was lowest cumulative TIME across all four events, not points; the documentary title 'Every Second Counts' comes from this format. Saturday's three events (Workout A thruster/pull-up, Workout B deadlift/burpee, The Hill Run) ran simultaneously in three rounds of nine heats (9:00 AM, 1:00 PM, 5:00 PM waves per the official master schedule); each athlete emailed a preferred order and completed all three in their assigned rotation, so there is no single canonical event sequence for Saturday. A scaled division existed: athletes could request reduced thruster/deadlift loads (e.g. 45-75 lb thrusters, jumping pull-ups) and were flagged 'X' (X=SCALED) in the results, separately from 'A' athletes, whom the official corrected-results PDF legends define as 'A=IN CONTENTION' (men) / 'A=CONTENDER' (women); DNF/no-show athletes were assigned placeholder times (12:01 for the capped Saturday WODs, 15:01 for the final event). Sunday's final event was kept secret until Saturday evening after all three events were done; it ran in heats, with the contenders' final heats using a staggered (pursuit) start based on each athlete's cumulative Saturday time, so the first across the line won the Games. Field counts here are the rows in the official corrected results PDFs (196 men, 91 women) and include scaled-division and DNF athletes. Prize money per the official June 2008 announcement: $1,500 each for Top Male and Top Female CrossFitter plus another $2,000 spread across other placings and events (Wikipedia instead states each event winner won $1,500 - conflict noted, official contemporaneous source preferred).
years.yearSummary: The second CrossFit Games returned to the Castro family ranch in Aromas with an open, ~300-cap field and a unique cumulative-time scoring system in which every second across four short events counted equally. Saturday packed three couplet/sprint tests - a chest-to-bar 'Fran' (21-15-9 thrusters and chest-to-bar pull-ups), a 5x(5 deadlifts + 10 burpees) couplet, and a roughly 750 m off-trail hill sprint - into rotating heats, and the surprise finale of 30 squat clean and jerks was only announced Saturday night. Sunday's staggered-start final heat produced the Games' first great chase narrative: Jason Khalipa, eighth and about 1:27 down after day one, ran through the field with the fastest clean-and-jerk time (2:46) to win, while Caity Matter overhauled Tanya Wagner by 10 seconds for the women's title. The year introduced the chest-to-bar pull-up standard, thrusters, burpees, and the squat clean and jerk to Games competition, and was documented in the film 'Every Second Counts'.

events.name: Workout A
events.description:
21-15-9 reps for time of:
Thrusters (95 lb men / 65 lb women)
Chest-to-bar pull-ups

12-minute time limit.

Thruster: front squat to full overhead lockout each rep. Pull-up standard required the chest to physically touch the bar (the first time CrossFit used the chest-to-bar standard in competition); any style of kip including butterfly was allowed per the official standards video. Scaled-division athletes could request lighter thrusters (e.g. 45-75 lb) and jumping pull-ups.
events.notes: Fran with the brand-new chest-to-bar standard, which contemporaries predicted would produce 'much slower than record Fran times'. The modern games.crossfit.com card lists simply 'Pull-ups', but the 2008 standards video, contemporaneous athlete comments on the official Games blog, and Wikipedia all confirm chest-to-bar was required. Saturday's three events had no fixed order: each athlete did this WOD in one of three heat rounds (9:00 AM, 1:00 PM, or 5:00 PM waves). Top-5 men: Spealler 3:01, Everett 3:29, Frausto 3:30, Lowy 3:30, Tincher 3:33. Top-5 women: Leipper 5:06, Mounsey 5:17, Gentry 5:43, Wagner 5:55, Hamilton 6:28.

events.name: Workout B
events.description:
5 rounds for time of:
5 Deadlifts (275 lb men / 185 lb women)
10 Burpees

12-minute time limit.

Deadlift standard (official rules clarification, July 4, 2008): any stance is acceptable as long as the hands are outside the knees (no sumo grip-inside-knees). Burpee standard (official addendum, July 3, 2008): hips must open fully during the jump at the top of each burpee. Scaled-division athletes could request lighter deadlifts (e.g. 135-250 lb).
events.notes: First appearance of burpees at the Games (deadlifts had appeared in the 2007 CrossFit Total). Contested in rotating heats like the other Saturday events. Top-5 men: Chan 2:33, Griffin 2:35, Khalipa 2:37, Thomas 2:41, Spealler 2:41. Top-5 women: Dibiase 3:23, Matter 3:53, Rydh 3:54, Orr 4:03, Wagner 4:10.

events.name: The Hill Run
events.description:
For time:
Run approximately 750 meters - a steep, off-trail run over rough terrain up the hillside at the Ranch in Aromas.

20-minute time limit (official), though winning times were under 3:30.
events.notes: Extraordinarily tight spread: the official Games blog noted only 38 seconds separated 1st from 38th in the men's run (eventual champion Jason Khalipa was that 38th at 3:58). Exact course profile (one-way vs out-and-back, elevation gain) was never published; contemporaneous comments describe walking the hill as serious business ('Now I know why goat herders have dogs'). Top-5 men: O'Connor 3:20, Gray 3:22, Spealler 3:22, Berry 3:25, Blomberg 3:25. Top-5 women: Tillman 4:24, Pryor 4:27, Xavier 4:33, Wagner 4:35, S. Spealler 4:39.

events.name: Sunday's Workout
events.description:
For time:
30 Squat Clean and Jerks (155 lb men / 100 lb women)

Official standard (posted July 5, 2008, the night before): 'The barbell goes from ground to overhead, passing through a front squat in which the crease of the hip passes below the height of the kneecap. The finish position is with the arms, hips and knees fully extended, arms overhead, with at least a portion of the ear visible in front of the arm. Dropping the barbell is acceptable.' A squat-clean-to-thruster technique was explicitly briefed to all competitors as an allowable method of completing the work.
events.notes: The surprise final event, announced Saturday evening after all three day-1 events were complete (met with 'more than a few groans and several cheers'). Early heats ran straight for time (Max Mormont's 3:24 was 'the time to beat' through midday); the contenders' final heats used a staggered pursuit start seeded by cumulative Saturday time, so the first athlete across the line won the Games. Khalipa started roughly 1:27 behind day-1 leader Chris Spealler (9:04 through Saturday) and posted the fastest time of the entire event (2:46) for a come-from-behind title at 13:17 total; Spealler faded to 7:27 and 10th overall. Caity Matter (3:30, also the fastest women's time) ran down Tanya Wagner's 1:00 head start to win by 10 seconds, 19:10 to 19:20. Some Khalipa critics questioned his squat depth/technique; CrossFit HQ publicly noted the squat-clean-to-thruster method was legal. No time cap was published; DNF placeholder times of 15:01 in the official results suggest an effective ~15-minute limit, but this is not confirmed. Top-5 men: Khalipa 2:46, Mormont 3:24, Thiel 3:52, C. Banks 4:14, Everett 4:17. Top-5 women: Matter 3:30, Holmes 4:14, Xavier 4:14, Wagner 4:40, Mounsey 5:11.

years.formatNotes: First year athletes had to qualify through regional qualifiers; 74 men and 72 women started, by far the largest Games field to date. Placement-points scoring: 1 point for 1st, 2 for 2nd, etc., lowest total wins. Progressive cuts: the bottom 10 men and 10 women were cut after Event 2 (Deadlift Ladder) and again after Event 4 (Row/Hammer Stake); only the top 16 men and 16 women after Event 5 (Couplet) advanced to Sunday's final three events. Saturday (July 11) held five events, Sunday (July 12) three. First year of drug testing at the Games and first year of the Affiliate Cup team competition (teams competed Friday and Sunday; not covered in this file). Each individual champion received $5,000. Note: Wikipedia's body text calls July 10 'Saturday', but July 10, 2009 was a Friday (team events); the five individual events ran Saturday July 11 and the last three Sunday July 12.
years.yearSummary: The third CrossFit Games, and the last truly rustic year at the Aromas ranch, opened with a shock: a roughly 7 km hill run that buried 2008 champion Jason Khalipa (72nd of 74) and announced that broad capacity, not gym fitness alone, would decide the title. Dave Castro's programming leaned hard into the unknown and unknowable - a 20-bar deadlift ladder, a sandbag sprint up the hill, and a sledgehammer stake-drive sandwiched between 500 m rows. Sunday introduced the Games' first 1RM snatch, a savage parallette-HSPU triplet, and a 10-movement final chipper. Finland's Mikko Salo, in his first Games, won the final event to take the men's title with relentless consistency (no finish worse than 32nd), while Tanya Wagner rode top-11 finishes in every event to the women's crown; 18-year-old rookie Annie Thorisdottir won the sandbag sprint but fell from podium contention to 11th when the final chipper's muscle-ups stopped her cold. Wall balls, squat snatches, kettlebell swings, GHD sit-ups, handstand push-ups, muscle-ups, toes-to-bar, box jumps and double-unders all made their Games debuts in 2009, sketching the template the sport still uses.

events.name: 7k Hill Run
events.description:
For time:
Run approx. 7 km (some period accounts say 7.2 km) over steep, hilly ranch terrain at Aromas.
Cross-country course on dirt trails and hills around The Ranch; same course for men and women.
events.notes: Longest run in Games history to that point and a deliberate ambush of pure-gym athletes. Defending champion Jason Khalipa reportedly collapsed multiple times and finished 72nd of 74 (54:35.5). Exact distance is variously reported as 7.0-7.2 km; the official archive simply calls it a '7-k Hill Run'.

events.name: Deadlift Ladder
events.description:
Deadlift ladder for max load:
1 deadlift every 30 seconds, advancing along a line of 20 pre-loaded bars in 10-lb increments.
Men: 315 lb up to 505 lb.
Women: 185 lb up to 375 lb.
A period spectator account describes the 30-second window as 20 seconds to complete the lift plus 10 seconds to rotate to the next bar. Score = heaviest successful deadlift.
events.notes: First barbell-ladder format at the Games. winnerMen is null because there was no single men's winner: the official leaderboard shows a 16-way tie at rank 1, all 16 men finishing the entire ladder at 505 lb - Moe Kelsey, Jason Khalipa, Peter Egyed, DJ Wickham, Spencer Hendel, Jeremy Thiel, Jerome Perryman, Graham Holmberg, J.C. Nessa, Rob Orlando, Jordan Holland, Josh Everett, Lance Mosley, Scott Lewis, David Lipson and Jason Neago. Cyndi Frieling alone topped the women's ladder at 375 lb. Chris Spealler, the run winner, placed 71st of 74 here. The bottom 10 men and 10 women were cut after this event.

events.name: Sandbag Hill Sprint
events.description:
For time:
170-meter sprint up the hill at The Ranch carrying sandbags.
Men: two 35-lb sandbags (70 lb total).
Women: one 35-lb sandbag.
Bags could be carried any way; athletes sprinted straight up the natural hillside that formed the stadium's backdrop.
events.notes: First odd-object/loaded-carry event at the Games. Icelanders swept it: Sveinbjorn Sveinbjornsson won the men's race and 18-year-old rookie Annie Thorisdottir (future two-time champion) won the women's. Distance reported as 170 m on the official archive; one period account says 'almost 175 m'.

events.name: Row/Hammer Stake
events.description:
For time:
Row 500 meters (Concept2 erg)
Drive a blunt steel stake into packed ground with a sledgehammer until no more than 6 inches remains above the ground
Row 500 meters
Men: 4-foot stake. Women: 3-foot stake. Sledgehammer reported as 8 lb (CrossFit Journal retrospective).
events.notes: Quintessential 'unknown and unknowable' test - most athletes had never swung a sledgehammer; accuracy mattered more than power. Sarah Dunsmore took her second event win of the day. The bottom 10 men and 10 women were cut after this event. The 8-lb hammer weight comes from a 2015 CrossFit Journal retrospective ('Hammer Time') and is not stated on the official archive page.

events.name: Wall Ball/Squat Snatch Couplet
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
30 Wall-ball shots (20-lb ball for men, 14-lb for women; target reported at 10.5 feet)
30 Squat snatches (75 lb men / 45 lb women)
20-minute time cap (per secondary accounts; not printed on the official archive - see notes). Period accounts note the snatch had to initiate with the barbell below the knees; power snatch + overhead squat was permitted.
events.notes: Brutal volume for 2009: 90 wall balls and 90 snatches. Khalipa won using a power snatch + overhead squat strategy. After this event the field was cut to the top 16 men and 16 women for Sunday. SOURCING - 20-min cap: the official archive prints no time cap; the 20-minute figure comes from secondary sourcing (WODwell) but is strongly corroborated by the official leaderboard, where exactly 13 men and 15 women are recorded DNF and the slowest finishers are 19:37.0 (men) and 19:58.4 (women), all under 20:00. CONFLICT - movement/load: one period source (Snoridge CrossFit) describes the barbell movement as 'Hang Squat Snatch' at 75/55 lb (i.e. 55 lb for women), conflicting with the official archive's 'Squat Snatches (75/45 lb.)'; the official 75/45 lb is recorded here. The 10.5-ft target height comes from period/retrospective accounts, not the official archive; the women's target height is not separately documented.

events.name: Max Snatch
events.description:
Barbell snatch, 1-rep max.
Athletes went out in heats of about 10, each with their own barbell, and had 10 minutes to build to a max single snatch (ground to overhead, bar locked out; any snatch style - unlimited attempts within the window).
events.notes: First 1RM snatch event in Games history and first single-lift max event since the 2007 CrossFit Total. Unlike weightlifting meets, attempts were unlimited inside the 10-minute window and athletes loaded their own bars. Jason Khalipa was 2nd at 225 lb; Tanya Wagner was 2nd at 135 lb, protecting her overall lead.

events.name: The Triplet
events.description:
AMRAP in 8 minutes of:
4 Handstand push-ups (performed on parallettes per period accounts - a deficit, with strict depth standard)
8 Kettlebell swings (32 kg / 70 lb men, 24 kg / 53 lb women; bell swung to full vertical overhead, bottom of the bell facing the sky)
12 GHD sit-ups
Score = total reps.
events.notes: The deficit parallette HSPU standard wrecked the field: four of the 16 women finalists recorded no score (DNF, unable to complete the opening handstand push-ups) and one finalist managed only 2 reps; men's scores ranged from 172 down to 27. Parallette and overhead-swing standards come from a period spectator account; the official archive lists the movements and KB weights only.

events.name: The Chipper
events.description:
For time:
15 Cleans (155 lb men / 100 lb women)
30 Toes-to-bars
30 Box jumps (24-in men / 20-in women)
15 Muscle-ups (women's reps disputed: official archive says 15, several retrospectives say 10)
30 Dumbbell push presses (pair of 40-lb DBs men / 25-lb DBs women)
30 Double-unders
15 Thrusters (135 lb men / 95 lb women)
30 Pull-ups
30 Burpees
300-foot Overhead walking lunge (45-lb plate men / 25-lb plate women)
events.notes: Mikko Salo won the event to clinch the championship in his Games debut; Charity Vale's event win vaulted her to 2nd overall. Annie Thorisdottir, in podium contention, hit the muscle-ups, got the first muscle-up of her life to roars from the crowd, but could not complete another and DNF'd, dropping to 11th. Five men (including snatch winner Jeff Leonard) are recorded DNF, and two women (Laura DeMarco, Tamara Holmes) are marked CUT for this event on the official leaderboard. Time cap, if any, is not documented (slowest recorded finishers: 27:37 men, 33:58 women). CONFLICT: the official workout archive lists 15 muscle-ups for both men and women, while multiple retrospectives (Men's Journal, bfriendlyfitness) say women did 10; the official figure is recorded here.

years.formatNotes: Fourth CrossFit Games and the first held at the Home Depot Center in Carson after three years at the Aromas ranch. Qualification was a new two-stage process: Sectionals feeding into Regionals (precursor to the Open). 45 men and 41 women competed (the official leaderboard lists 45 registered women; Wikipedia reports 41 started). Scoring was placement-equals-points: 1st = 1 point, 2nd = 2 points, lowest total wins. No workout was announced in advance - athletes learned each event roughly an hour before contesting it (the final three were revealed heat by heat with under a minute to prepare), though organizers guaranteed everyone a minimum of four workouts. Nine separately scored events: Amanda (Friday night), Pyramid Double Helen plus an immediately attached 1RM shoulder-to-overhead scored as two events (Saturday morning), Deadlift-Pistol-Double-under (Saturday afternoon, field cut to 24 after it), Sandbag Move (Saturday night), Cleans-Handstand Push-ups (Sunday morning, field cut to 16 after it), and the three back-to-back Finals (Sunday afternoon). Champions earned 25,000 dollars. The masters division (50+) debuted this year. Dave Castro announced that all individual workouts from Event 3 onward took place in the main stadium.
years.yearSummary: The 2010 Games moved CrossFit from a dusty ranch to a professional stadium and introduced the benchmark 'Amanda' - the first workout ever named for a Games athlete, honoring Amanda Miller, the 2009 competitor who died of melanoma in April 2010. Programming blended classic couplets with stadium-scale work: a pyramided double Helen straight into a 90-second 1RM shoulder-to-overhead, a heavy AMRAP with the Games debut of pistols, a sandbag-and-wheelbarrow odd-object task, ring handstand push-ups, and a three-part final featuring the first Games rope climbs. Rookie Rich Froning Jr. led entering the last event but, unable to use a foot lock, climbed his ropes essentially legless, blew up, and finished 12th in the event - handing Graham Holmberg the title by three points in one of the most famous collapses in Games history. Kristan Clever was dominant on the women's side (five event wins or ties), holding off 20-year-old Icelandic newcomer Annie Thorisdottir, while Chris Spealler finally reached the podium in his fourth Games.

events.name: Amanda
events.description:
9-7-5 reps for time of:
Muscle-ups
Squat snatches (135 lb. men / 95 lb. women)
12-minute time cap.
Athletes who did not finish within the cap were ranked by total reps completed.
events.notes: Debut of the 'Amanda' benchmark - the first workout ever named in honor of a Games athlete, dedicated to Amanda Miller (55th at the 2009 Games), who died of melanoma on April 23, 2010, aged 24. Contested Friday night after an F/A-18 flyover and opening ceremonies, with a video tribute before the final women's heat. Spealler traded leads with Jason Khalipa, who faltered on the final snatches; Neal Maddox was 2nd (3:46) and Rich Froning Jr. 3rd (3:47). Camille Leblanc-Bazinet was 2nd for the women (7:02) and Christy Phillips 3rd (7:04). Only 11 women finished within the 12-minute cap. The same-night blog recap reported Clever's time as 5:08, but the official leaderboard and the Amanda Miller tribute post both record 5:04.

events.name: Pyramid Double Helen
events.description:
For time (22-minute cap):
Run 1,200 meters
63 kettlebell swings (1.5 pood men / 1 pood women)
36 pull-ups
Run 800 meters
42 kettlebell swings
24 pull-ups
Run 400 meters
21 kettlebell swings
12 pull-ups
(1.5 pood = 53 lb; 1 pood = 35 lb. Within 90 seconds of finishing, athletes moved directly to the separately scored 1-rep-max Shoulder-to-Overhead.)
events.notes: A pyramided double-volume version of the benchmark Helen, announced at 7 a.m. Saturday and contested at the Home Depot Center track facility (events moved into the main stadium from Event 3 on). The blog recap nicknamed it 'Hell-In'. Chris Spealler was 2nd for the men (17:02), Peter Egyed 3rd (17:34). Annie Thorisdottir broke first on the round-2 kettlebell swings in a head-to-head duel with Kristan Clever but recovered to win; Clever was 2nd (18:23) and Samantha Briggs 3rd (18:30). The recap reported Thorisdottir's time as 17:52; the official leaderboard shows 17:53. Many athletes tore their hands here, which affected later events.

events.name: Shoulder-to-Overhead
events.description:
Within 90 seconds of completing Pyramid Double Helen:
1-rep-max shoulder-to-overhead.
Barbell taken from the ground; any style of getting the bar overhead was permitted (push press, push jerk, split jerk - behind-the-neck and snatch-grip jerks were allowed).
Score is the heaviest successful lift.
events.notes: Scored as a separate event despite being attached to Pyramid Double Helen (the pairing was announced as Event 2a/2b). D.J. Wickham put 325 lb overhead even after failing to finish 2a within its cap and ranks 1st on the official leaderboard; Ben Smith was 2nd (295 lb) and Graham Holmberg 3rd (285 lb). Jerome Perryman hit 275 lb with a snatch-grip behind-the-neck jerk. Kristan Clever's 205 lb came via a behind-the-head jerk; Jessica Pamanian was 2nd (195 lb). Rich Froning Jr. managed only 245 lb (tied 13th), and Camille Leblanc-Bazinet could not pull the bar from the floor after the runs and settled for 125 lb - the 90-second window after a 17-22 minute workout was the test.

events.name: Deadlift-Pistol-Double-under
events.description:
As many rounds as possible in 7 minutes of:
7 deadlifts (315 lb. men / 205 lb. women)
Sprint across the court
14 pistols (alternating one-legged squats)
21 double-unders
Sprint back
Score is total reps completed.
events.notes: First appearance of pistols in the individual Games competition (they had debuted a day earlier in the Affiliate Cup). Froning pulled away in the last minute to tie Austin Malleolo at 242 reps; Graham Holmberg and Brandon Phillips tied for 3rd at 237. On the women's side Thorisdottir out-dueled Kristan Clever again, 234 to 227 (Clever tied with Christy Phillips). Defending champion Mikko Salo struggled with double-unders. Many athletes had bandaged hands from tears suffered in Pyramid Double Helen. The field was cut to 24 men and 24 women after this event.

events.name: Sandbag Move
events.description:
For time:
Move 600 lb. (men) / 370 lb. (women) of sandbags from the top of the stadium stairs: carry the bags down the stairs, over a wall and into a wheelbarrow, push the wheelbarrow across the stadium floor, then move the bags back over a wall and carry them up the stairs to the finish.
Athletes chose how many bags to carry per trip; multiple trips up and down the stairs were allowed.
events.notes: Saturday-night homage to the 2009 Aromas sandbag hill sprint, contested by the 24 remaining athletes per division. Strategy mattered: trips, bag distribution, and wheelbarrow stacking. Matt Chan dumped his wheelbarrow twice; Brandon Phillips had two dumps plus a broken wheelbarrow but finished to a huge ovation. Hackenbruck (a former construction worker) was the first man under 7 minutes; Rich Froning Jr. was 2nd (7:14) and Mikko Salo 3rd (7:24). Thorisdottir cleared the wall easily and won by 34 seconds over Christy Phillips (8:38), with Rebecca Voigt 3rd (8:59); Kristan Clever struggled with the wheelbarrow and wall and placed 20th (11:20), dropping the overall lead to Thorisdottir. The official workout page omits the wheelbarrow; the on-site recap documents it ('down a set of stairs, over a wall, into a wheelbarrow, across the stadium, over the wall and up the stairs'), and CrossFit's 2015 retrospective 'Whitecaps and Wheelbarrows' (games.crossfit.com, July 22, 2015) independently corroborates it - hardware-store wheelbarrows used to transport the loads across the stadium floor, assembled by Rory McKernan, Miranda Oldroyd and Pat Sherwood. That retrospective also reports the event's 20-minute time cap (no cap appeared on the original workout page) and confirms the 600/370-lb loads and the 6:57/8:04 winning times.

events.name: Cleans-Handstand Push-ups
events.description:
7 rounds for time of:
3 cleans (205 lb. men / 135 lb. women)
4 handstand push-ups (men on rings, women on the floor)
12-minute time cap.
events.notes: Games debut of ring handstand push-ups (men only; women did standard HSPU). Holmberg beat Chris Spealler (4:27) by a single second in a finish so close judges double-checked their stopwatches - one of his two event wins en route to the title; Ben Smith was 3rd (4:57). Clever 'annihilated' the workout, winning by 32 seconds over Valerie Voboril (4:09), with Heather Bergeron 3rd (5:01). Many men tumbled from the rings (including 325-lb jerker D.J. Wickham), and five women in Heat 1 did not finish. The field was cut to 16 per division after this event, setting up the finals.

events.name: The Final 1
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
30 push-ups with hand release
Over the wall
21 overhead squats (95 lb. men / 65 lb. women)
7-minute time cap.
Athletes climbed over a wall between stations (the official recap describes a wall climb 'between each element'). Athletes capped were scored by reps completed.
events.notes: First of three back-to-back finals workouts for the last 16 athletes, who had been sequestered under the stands since 1 p.m. and were given each task heat by heat with under a minute to prepare; each part was scored as a separate event. No woman finished - Clever got further than anyone (138 reps; CrossFit's main-site repost describes her score as 2 rounds plus 30 push-ups). Froning won in 6:55, per CrossFit's main-site repost of the final as the Workout of the Day for July 23, 2010 ('Part A: Rich Froning Jr. 6:55'); the official leaderboard encodes that finish as '163 reps' (reps plus a time bonus, exceeding the nominal 156-159 rep total), with Chris Spealler 2nd at 156. The same-day recap loosely credited Spealler with the win, but the published final points totals (Holmberg 48, Froning 51, Spealler 69) only reconcile with Froning winning this event.

events.name: The Final 2
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
30 toes-to-bars
21 ground-to-overheads (95 lb. men / 65 lb. women)
7-minute time cap.
Any method of taking the bar from ground to overhead was allowed. Athletes capped were scored by reps completed.
events.notes: Middle leg of the three-part final, started moments after The Final 1. Nobody in either division came close to finishing the 153 reps within 7 minutes - the event winners completed roughly two of the three rounds. Clever and Voboril tied at 106 reps for the women's win; Annie Thorisdottir was 3rd (96 reps). Ben Smith's 99 reps edged Graham Holmberg (96, 2nd), whose steadiness here protected his title charge; Chris Spealler scored 91 (5th). CrossFit's main-site repost of the final (Workout of the Day, July 23, 2010) corroborates both winning scores: 'Part B: Ben Smith 1 round + 18 ground to OH' (= 99 reps) and Kristan Clever '2 rounds + 4' (= 106 reps).

events.name: The Final 3
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
5 burpee wall jumps
3 rope climbs, 20-foot (men) / 2 rope climbs, 20-foot (women)
12-minute time cap.
Athletes capped were scored by reps completed; finishers were ranked by time.
events.notes: The event that decided the Games and the debut of rope climbs at the Games. Overall leader Rich Froning Jr., not knowing how to use a foot lock, did most of his climbs essentially legless, blew up his grip and arms, and finished 12th ('9 reps' on the leaderboard) - Graham Holmberg ground through his climbs, finished the workout, and won the title by 3 points. Ex-Marine Pat Burke was the day's first finisher (10:41) using a foot lock; Tommy Hackenbruck and Peter Egyed also finished, and Spealler won the event nearly two minutes faster than the day's best time. Thorisdottir, Julie Foucher, and Valerie Voboril (plus, per the leaderboard, Kristan Clever) finished for the women. Winning times (Spealler 8:32, Thorisdottir 7:34) are from CrossFit's own main-site repost of the three-part final as the Workout of the Day for July 23, 2010, which credits 'Part C: Chris Spealler 8:32, Annie Thorisdottir 7:34'. The official leaderboard instead displays encoded rep values for finishers ('231 reps' Spealler, '287 reps' Thorisdottir) that exceed the maximum 24/21 literal movement reps - reps plus an unpublished time-remaining bonus - so the leaderboard's rep figures for this event are display artifacts, not literal rep counts.

years.formatNotes: First year of the modern three-stage season: the worldwide Open (over 26,000 athletes, six weekly workouts) fed 17 Regionals, which qualified roughly 50 athletes per division to the Games. First year of the Reebok title sponsorship ('Reebok CrossFit Games') and a $250,000 first-place prize. Each event was worth 100 points to the winner; points dropped 5 per place through 6th (95, 90, 85, 80, 75), then 2 per place from 7th through 30th, then 1 per place beyond. Progressive cuts during the weekend: the official leaderboard shows 48 of 49 men and 45 of 47 women scored Event 1, and 47 men / 45 women scored Events 2-5 (not quite the full field: Rob Orlando was DNF in the swim, Mikko Salo withdrew after it with a burst eardrum, and Deborah Cordner Carson and Helga Torfadottir went unscored from Event 1 on); 35 men and 35 women contested Event 6 (Killer Kage), 24 contested Event 7 (Dog-Sled), and the final 12 per division contested Events 8-10 (The End 1-3). Note: Wikipedia phrases the cuts as coming 'after the 6th event' and 'after the 7th'; the leaderboard's scored-athlete counts (35 in Event 6, 24 in Event 7, 12 in Events 8-10) are recorded here as authoritative.
years.yearSummary: 2011 was the year the CrossFit Games became a season: the inaugural Open and Regionals funneled a true worldwide field into Carson, Reebok signed on as title sponsor, ESPN3 streamed the weekend, and the champions' checks jumped to $250,000. Dave Castro leaned into 'unknown and unknowable' programming - the Games opened off-site with an ocean swim event at Santa Monica beach (where 2009 champion Mikko Salo burst an eardrum and withdrew), and skills tests (softball throw, handstand walk, L-sit, max weighted pull-up, water-jug carry) plus new implements (Watt bikes, the Kage monkey-bar rig, the Rogue dog sled) debuted alongside classic barbell work. Rich Froning, the 2010 runner-up, won three events and avenged his 2010 rope-climb collapse by winning Rope-Clean, claiming the first of his four straight titles; Iceland's Annie Thorisdottir won three events herself to take the women's crown from Kristan Clever. Josh Bridges (men) and Sam Briggs (women) each won multiple events, and the weekend ended with The End, a three-part repeated chipper finale capped by a rope-assisted sled pull.

events.name: Beach
events.description:
For time:
210-meter ocean swim
1,500-meter soft-sand run
50 chest-to-bar pull-ups
100 hand-release push-ups
200 squats
1,500-meter soft-sand run

Same distances and reps for men and women. Contested off-site on the beach at Santa Monica: athletes swam out and around buoys in the ocean, ran 1,500 m down the soft sand, completed the pull-ups on temporary rigs, the push-ups and air squats on the beach, then ran 1,500 m back to the finish.
events.notes: First swim event in Games history and the first individual event held away from the main venue. 2009 champion Mikko Salo burst an eardrum during the ocean swim and withdrew from the competition. Navy SEAL Josh Bridges won the men's heat.

events.name: Skills 1
events.description:
Three tests:
1. Max L-sit for time (1 attempt)
2. Max-distance softball throw (2 attempts)
3. Max-distance handstand walk (1 attempt, with 1 mulligan if less than 5 yards)

Same tests for men and women, no external loading. Athletes were ranked in each test, and the sum of their three rankings determined their finish for the event (low sum wins); the event then paid out the standard 100-point scale like every other event.
events.notes: First of two ranked-skills events, part of 2011's 'unknown and unknowable' theme. Component-by-component results were not preserved on the official leaderboard, which records only final event points; the winning scores shown are event points, not raw marks.

events.name: Rope-Clean
events.description:
For time:
15-foot rope climb, 5 ascents
Clean and jerks, 5 reps (145 lb M / 115 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 4 ascents
Clean and jerks, 4 reps (165 lb M / 125 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 3 ascents
Clean and jerks, 3 reps (185 lb M / 135 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 2 ascents
Clean and jerks, 2 reps (205 lb M / 145 lb W)
15-foot rope climb, 1 ascent
Clean and jerk, 1 rep (225 lb M / 155 lb W)

Descending 5-4-3-2-1 couplet: 15 total rope ascents and 15 total clean and jerks, with the barbell load climbing 20 lb (men) / 10 lb (women) each round.
events.notes: Friday night stadium event. Rich Froning, whose inability to climb a rope cost him the 2010 title, won the event outright; both eventual champions (Froning and Thorisdottir) won it in their divisions.

events.name: Triplet Sprint
events.description:
For time:
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 50 yards
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 100 yards
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 150 yards
5 muscle-ups
10 deadlifts (245 lb M / 165 lb W)
15 GHD sit-ups
Sprint 200 yards

Four rounds of the muscle-up/deadlift/GHD triplet, with the sprint growing by 50 yards each round (500 yards of running total).

events.name: Skills 2
events.description:
Three tests:
1. 1-rep-max weighted chest-to-bar pull-up for load (2 minutes to establish)
2. 1-rep-max snatch for load (2 minutes to establish)
3. Jug carry for distance in 60 seconds (carry 2 weighted steel 5-gallon water jugs as far as possible)

Athletes were ranked in each test, and the sum of their three rankings determined their finish for the event (low sum wins), paying out the standard 100-point scale.
events.notes: The weight of the steel water jugs was never published on the official card. Documented component bests, all per the official Event 5 results article (games.crossfit.com/article/2011-games-individual-event-5-results): Lucas Parker's 130-lb weighted chest-to-bar pull-up (men), Lindsay Valenzuela's 165-lb snatch (women), and Elisabeth Akinwale's 364-ft jug carry (women's farthest; the article reads '364 feet even - and she turned around at the end of the field and walked back'). Winning scores shown are event points, not raw marks; the leaderboard preserved only final event placings.

events.name: Killer Kage
events.description:
Three rounds for time of:
7 front squats (225 lb M / 155 lb W)
Bike 700 meters
100-foot monkey bar traverse

Barbell taken from the ground. Athletes rode bikes on a 700-meter loop out of the stadium and back each round, then crossed the 100-foot 'Kage' monkey-bar rig.
events.notes: Saturday night event. First time bikes were used at the Games and debut of the 'Kage' monkey-bar rig. First post-cut event: only the top 35 men and 35 women contested it.

events.name: Dog-Sled
events.description:
For time:
Three rounds of:
30 double-unders
10 overhead squats (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
then, three rounds of:
10 handstand push-ups
40-foot sled push (sled + 385 lb M / sled + 275 lb W)

Back-to-back couplets: three rounds of the double-under/overhead-squat couplet, immediately followed by three rounds of handstand push-ups and a 40-foot push of a heavily loaded dog sled.
events.notes: Debut of the Rogue dog sled at the Games. Contested by the final 24 men and 24 women after the second cut.

events.name: The End 1
events.description:
Complete as many reps as possible in 3 minutes of:
20-calorie row
30 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball M / 14-lb ball W)
20 toes-to-bars
30 box jumps (24-inch box, men and women)
20 sumo deadlift high pulls (108-lb kettlebell M / 72-lb kettlebell W)
30 burpees
20 shoulder-to-overheads (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
Sled pull

First part of the three-part finale: athletes worked through the chipper from the top for 3 minutes, scored by total reps completed. 1 minute of rest before The End 2.
events.notes: Contested by the final 12 men and 12 women only. The End 1, 2 and 3 were three separately scored 100-point events run nearly back to back. Box height was 24 inches for both divisions. The closing sled pull's load and distance were never published on the official card; athletes pulled a sled in hand over hand by rope.

events.name: The End 2
events.description:
Complete as many reps as possible in 6 minutes of:
20-calorie row
30 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball M / 14-lb ball W)
20 toes-to-bars
30 box jumps (24-inch box, men and women)
20 sumo deadlift high pulls (108-lb kettlebell M / 72-lb kettlebell W)
30 burpees
20 shoulder-to-overheads (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
Sled pull

Second part of the finale, begun after 1 minute of rest: athletes restarted the same chipper from the top and worked for 6 minutes, scored by total reps completed. 2 minutes of rest before The End 3.
events.notes: Contested by the final 12 men and 12 women only. Each part restarted the chipper from the beginning rather than continuing from the previous stopping point.

events.name: The End 3
events.description:
For time:
20-calorie row
30 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball M / 14-lb ball W)
20 toes-to-bars
30 box jumps (24-inch box, men and women)
20 sumo deadlift high pulls (108-lb kettlebell M / 72-lb kettlebell W)
30 burpees
20 shoulder-to-overheads (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
Sled pull

Third and final part, begun after 2 minutes of rest: the complete chipper for time, finishing with the rope-assisted sled pull across the stadium floor. First athlete to finish the eight stations won the event and the 2011 season ended at the sled.
events.notes: Contested by the final 12 men and 12 women only. Rich Froning (8th, 14:10) and Annie Thorisdottir (3rd, 13:56) protected their leads through the finale to win their first titles. Froning called the closing sled pull the most miserable part of the weekend: 'I had no core left, no arms left.'

years.formatNotes: 15 scored individual events. Two-tier relative scoring: most events used a 100-point table (1st=100, 2nd=95, 3rd=90 ... 30th=27); three short tests (Broad Jump, Ball Toss, Sprint) used a 50-point table (1st=50, 2nd=48, 3rd=46 ... 30th=17). Ties took the higher placement. Time-capped events added a 1-second penalty per rep not completed at the cap. Max-effort events awarded 0.01 partial units per rep of a secondary movement (e.g. deadlifts in the Clean Ladder) as tiebreaks. The point tables (including 30th=27 and 30th=17), the tie rule and the one-second-per-missed-rep cap penalty are all stated verbatim on the official 'Scoring the 2012 Reebok CrossFit Games' page (archived July 9, 2012; see sources). The Games opened Wednesday July 11 with three events held off-site at the Camp Pendleton Marine Corps base (closed to spectators); Thursday was a rest day; competition resumed Friday-Sunday at the Home Depot Center. All 46 men and 45 women competed through the Saturday Clean Ladder, then the field was cut to 36 for the Chipper, 24 for Double Banger, 18 for Elizabeth, 15 for Isabel and 12 for Fran. This was the earliest pre-release of events in Games history (most workouts published July 6). Live coverage streamed on ESPN3 (Friday-Sunday, July 13-15) for the second straight year - ESPN3 coverage began in 2011 - and ESPN2 exclusively televised the Games as a 17-episode series beginning September 11, 2012.
years.yearSummary: The 2012 Reebok CrossFit Games stretched the test far beyond the stadium: athletes were opened with a surprise-location triathlon (ocean swim, bike, trail run) and a head-to-head Marine Corps obstacle course at Camp Pendleton, the first Games events ever staged off-site at a military base and the first to include cycling. Programming then swung from pure outliers (a standing broad jump, a 2-4 lb GHD ball toss, a 300-yard shuttle sprint) to new implements and movements including bar muscle-ups, split snatches, football-style sled drives, burpee muscle-ups and the sledgehammer-driven Banger, before closing with the classic benchmark girls Elizabeth, Isabel and Fran contested back-to-back-to-back with rolling cuts. Rich Froning won 3 of the final 5 events (the Chipper, Elizabeth and Isabel) to repeat as champion by 114 points, and Annie Thorisdottir repeated on the women's side to become the first two-time women's champion. Camille Leblanc-Bazinet's 2:35.3 in the final Fran was faster than the men's winning time.

events.name: Pendleton 1
events.description:
Triathlon race at Camp Pendleton Marine Corps base (8:00-11:30 a.m.):
Swim 700 +/- meters in the ocean (fins provided)
Bike 8 +/- kilometers (course included roughly 400 m of soft sand)
Run 11 +/- kilometers on dirt road with 1,400+ ft of elevation gain

Pendleton 1 was scored by order of arrival at a checkpoint approximately 150 meters into the run (i.e. effectively after the swim and bike legs). There was no scheduled rest; the race continued straight into the run, which was scored separately as Pendleton 2. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: First Games events held off-site at a military installation, and the first cycling at the Games. The Pendleton events were not part of the July 6 public workout release; athletes learned the details shortly before racing on Wednesday morning. Closed to spectators, covered by live radio.

events.name: Pendleton 2
events.description:
Same continuous race as Pendleton 1, scored a second time:
Swim 700 +/- meters in the ocean (fins provided)
Bike 8 +/- kilometers (including roughly 400 m of soft sand)
Run 11 +/- kilometers on dirt road with 1,400+ ft of elevation gain

Pendleton 2 ranked athletes by total time to finish the entire swim-bike-run course. The Pendleton 1 checkpoint placement did not affect this score. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: One race, two scores: a single continuous triathlon produced both Pendleton 1 (checkpoint order) and Pendleton 2 (total time), each worth 100 points.

events.name: Obstacle Course
events.description:
Complete the Camp Pendleton School of Infantry obstacle course (walls, bars, ropes, logs and other military obstacles), contested as a 3-round bracketed tournament (12:30-3:30 p.m.):
Four athletes raced head-to-head per heat; the top finisher from each heat advanced to the next round, with wildcards filling out brackets.
Final placing: positions 1-4 by finishing order in the final round; positions 5-16 by second-round times; positions 17 and below by first-round times. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Scores are in seconds (a shortened section of the SOI course; winning runs were roughly 33-36 seconds). Spencer Hendel beat Kenneth Leverich, Rich Froning and Pat Burke in the men's final after setting the day's fastest men's time of 35.39 seconds, surpassing Leverich's earlier 35.9 (per the official 'Pendleton Report: O-Course Assault' recap, cited in sources). An obstacle course would not return to the Games until 2017.

events.name: Broad Jump
events.description:
Standing broad jump for maximum distance.
Three attempts; athletes ranked by their furthest jump.
Contested Friday morning (individual competition opened with the broad jump at 10:30 a.m.). Worth 50 points.
events.notes: Schrader's winning jump was 9 ft 9 in. One of three 50-point events (the others were Ball Toss and Sprint).

events.name: Ball Toss
events.description:
Sitting in the GHD (glute-ham developer), athletes threw as many medicine balls as far as possible (overhead backward toss for distance).
Men: 4 lb medicine balls
Women: 2 lb medicine balls
Scored in points based on throw distance. Contested on the track (11:30 a.m.-2:20 p.m.); immediately after the Ball Toss, athletes reset together for the Track Triplet. Worth 50 points.
events.notes: The official description does not specify the number of balls thrown or the time window; the published score is a point total based on distance (e.g. men's winner 72 pt). Paired in the same heat block with the Track Triplet.

events.name: Track Triplet
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
8 Split snatches, alternating legs (115 / 75 lb)
7 Bar muscle-ups
Run 400 meters

Athletes ranked by time. Contested on the track immediately after the Ball Toss. Worth 100 points.
Time cap: 13 minutes.
events.notes: Split snatches with alternating legs and bar muscle-ups both debuted at the Games here. Dan Tyminski's 8:03.2 from an early heat held up for the win; Julie Foucher won the women's race over Kristan Clever (9:02.4).

events.name: Medball-HSPU
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
8 Medicine-ball cleans (150 / 80 lb ball)
100 foot Medicine-ball carry
7 Parallette handstand push-ups
100 foot Medicine-ball carry

Contested Friday evening in the stadium (6:00-8:05 p.m.). Worth 100 points.
Time cap: 10 minutes.
events.notes: This event was listed as TBA in the July 6 release and announced during Games week. Annie Thorisdottir's 5:04.1 was faster than the men's winning time.

events.name: Sprint
events.description:
300-yard shuttle sprint for time:
Run to the 50-yard line and back
Run to the 100-yard line and back

Athletes ranked by time. Contested on the track (10:50 a.m.-1:40 p.m.); immediately after the sprint, athletes reset together for the Rope-Sled event. Worth 50 points.
events.notes: Nate Schrader swept both pure athleticism tests, winning the Broad Jump and the Sprint.

events.name: Rope-Sled
events.description:
5 rounds for time of:
20 foot Rope climb, 1 ascent
20 yard Sled drive

Athletes drove the padded football-style sled 100 yards total in 20-yard increments. The men's sleds had 90 pounds added (no added load was published for the women's sleds). Contested on the track immediately after the Sprint. Worth 100 points.
Time cap: 13 minutes.
events.notes: The 20-foot rope returned (infamous from 2010) and football sled drives debuted. Official description specifies added weight only for the men's sleds; women appear to have driven the unloaded padded sled.

events.name: Clean Ladder
events.description:
1-rep Clean every 30 seconds with progressively heavier barbells.
Men's bars (lb): 245, 255, 265, 275, 285, 295, 305, 315, 325, 335, 345, 355, 365, 375, 385
Women's bars (lb): 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 195, 200, 205, 210, 215, 220, 225, 230, 235

Athletes ranked by the weight of their heaviest successful clean. After attempting and failing a clean, partial credit (0.01 per rep) was awarded for each additional deadlift completed, as a tiebreaker. Contested in the stadium (4:00-5:10 p.m.). Worth 100 points. The top 36 athletes overall after this event advanced.
events.notes: Score decimals are deadlift tiebreak units (0.01 per deadlift after the failed clean). Neal Maddox won at 365 lb over Jason Khalipa (355.10) and Marcus Hendren (355.06). Elisabeth Akinwale and Lindsey Valenzuela both topped the women's ladder at 235 lb, with Akinwale winning on the tiebreak (235.05 vs 235.02).

events.name: Chipper
events.description:
For time:
10 Overhead squats (155 / 105 lb)
10 Box jump overs (24 / 20 in box)
10 Fat-bar thrusters (135 / 95 lb)
10 Power cleans (205 / 125 lb)
10 Toes-to-bars
10 Burpee muscle-ups
10 Toes-to-bars
10 Power cleans (205 / 125 lb)
10 Fat-bar thrusters (135 / 95 lb)
10 Box jump overs (24 / 20 in box)
10 Overhead squats (155 / 105 lb)

Contested Saturday evening in the stadium (6:10-8:20 p.m.) by the top 36 athletes. Worth 100 points. The top 24 athletes overall after this event advanced to Sunday.
Time cap: 15 minutes.
events.notes: A mirrored (down-and-back) chipper of 110 reps. Burpee muscle-ups were introduced to the Games in this event, announced the night it was contested.

events.name: Double Banger
events.description:
For time:
50 Double-unders
Low banger
50 Double-unders
Down banger
50 Double-unders
Mid banger

The banger required driving a heavy weight along a sliding track by striking it with a sledgehammer. There were three tracks per lane: a low track, then a higher track struck downward through the legs, then another higher track at mid height. Contested Sunday morning in the stadium (11:00 a.m.-12:10 p.m.) by the top 24 athletes. Worth 100 points. The top 18 athletes overall after this event advanced to the Final.
Time cap: 9 minutes.
events.notes: The Banger apparatus (built by Rogue, inspired by firefighter-competition forcible-entry machines) debuted here; it was demoed in the stadium by UFC fighter Jason MacDonald when the event was announced the night before. Hammer and slide weights were not published.

events.name: Elizabeth
events.description:
21-15-9 reps for time of:
Cleans (135 / 95 lb)
Ring dips

First event of the three-part Final (Sunday 1:30-3:50 p.m.), contested by the top 18 athletes. Worth 100 points. The top 15 athletes overall after this event advanced to Isabel.
Time cap: 6 minutes.
events.notes: The Final was billed as three classic benchmark 'Girls' (Elizabeth, Isabel, Fran) run back-to-back-to-back with cuts after each, worth 3 x 100 points in total - the first time these benchmarks were contested at the Games.

events.name: Isabel
events.description:
For time:
30 Snatches (135 / 95 lb)

Second event of the three-part Final, contested by the top 15 athletes. Worth 100 points. The top 12 athletes overall after this event advanced to Fran.
Time cap: 6 minutes.
events.notes: Froning's 1:20.7 and Thorisdottir's 1:29.0 effectively sealed both titles heading into Fran.

events.name: Fran
events.description:
21-15-9 reps for time of:
Thrusters (95 / 65 lb)
Pull-ups

Final event of the Games, contested by the top 12 athletes. Worth 100 points.
Time cap: 6 minutes.
events.notes: Camille Leblanc-Bazinet's 2:35.3 was faster than the men's winning time. Rich Froning (1089 pts) and Annie Thorisdottir (1062 pts) closed out repeat championships; Thorisdottir became the first two-time women's champion.

years.formatNotes: Seventh CrossFit Games and the second at the renamed StubHub Center (formerly Home Depot Center). Qualification ran through the worldwide Open and 17 Regionals. 46 men and 44 women started (the official leaderboard lists 47 men, but Mikko Salo recorded no scores and withdrew before the first event). 12 separately scored events: a surprise pool swim and a half-marathon row on Wednesday, two days before the main competition opened, then three events each on Friday, Saturday and Sunday (no individual events Thursday, which belonged to Masters and teams). The half-marathon row was scored as two events: Row 1 at the 2,000-meter checkpoint and Row 2 for the full 21,097 meters. Every event was worth up to 100 points on the same placement-points table as 2012. All athletes competed through Event 10 (Sprint Chipper), after which only the top 30 men and top 30 women advanced to the final two events, The Cinco 1 and The Cinco 2, run back to back with exactly one minute between them. Athletes who did not finish within a time cap had one second added to their time for each repetition not completed.
years.yearSummary: The 2013 programming stretched the field in both directions: a surprise 500-yard pool swim with bar muscle-ups held offsite two days early, a half-marathon row that kept athletes on the erg for 80-95 minutes, and a strongman-flavored Burden Run that debuted the Pig, alongside pure sprints and a heavy clean-and-jerk ladder. Rich Froning opened with a 30th-place finish in the Pool, the worst Games event result of his career, then climbed all week and swept the final three events to clinch his third consecutive title (962 points to Jason Khalipa's 890). Britain's Samantha Briggs was relentless up front, winning Row 1 (in a tie), Row 2 and the Sprint Chipper and never falling out of contention, becoming the first champion from the UK; Lindsey Valenzuela was second and Valerie Voboril took third on a tiebreaker over Alessandra Pichelli after both finished with 818 points. New tests included bar muscle-ups, legless rope climbs, kettlebell-weighted pistols, burpees over a 6-foot wall and the Pig, and the top-30 cut before the finals was the first mid-competition cut since 2011. Josh Bridges won three events (Legless, Naughty Nancy and 2007) and rookie Amanda Goodman stole the clean-and-jerk ladder from last place overall with a 10-lb PR.

events.name: The Pool
events.description:
10 rounds for time of:
Swim 25 yards
3 Bar muscle-ups
Swim 25 yards
25-minute time cap.
Held Wednesday morning at the Woollett Aquatics Center in Irvine, Calif., two days before the main competition opened at the StubHub Center. Athletes swam a length, exited the water for 3 bar muscle-ups on a rig at the pool deck, then swam back, 10 times through (500 yards of swimming and 30 bar muscle-ups total).
events.notes: Surprise event announced shortly before the Games and contested before the official start. First pool swim in Games history (the 2011 and 2012 swims were in the ocean) and the Games debut of the bar muscle-up. Ben Smith was 2nd (10:28.5) and Josh Bridges 3rd (10:59.9) for the men; Kara Webb 2nd (13:55.9) and Rory Zambard 3rd (14:06.5) for the women. Rich Froning finished 30th (14:02.1), the worst Games event finish of his career to that point, setting up his comeback storyline. The official leaderboard spells the women's winner 'Michele Letendre' (often written 'Michelle' in recaps).

events.name: Row 1
events.description:
Row 21,097 meters for time.
Row 1 was the first scored segment of the half-marathon row, contested Wednesday afternoon on Concept2 ergs inside the VELO Sports Center velodrome. Athletes received points based on their time at the 2,000-meter checkpoint. There was no scheduled rest at the checkpoint; the race continued immediately as part of Row 2.
events.notes: Scored as a separate 100-point event at the 2K mark of the half-marathon row; finishing order here had no bearing on Row 2 scoring. Athletes had to gamble on pacing a 2K sprint at the front of a 21,097-meter race. Briggs and former collegiate rower Ladeairous tied at 7:17.0 for the women; Rich Froning was 2nd for the men (6:34.5) and Simon Paquette 3rd (6:35.9). The 2-hour overall cap applied to the full distance, not this segment.

events.name: Row 2
events.description:
Row 21,097 meters (a half marathon) for time.
Row 2 was scored as the total time to complete the entire 21,097 meters, inclusive of the Row 1 segment. Finishing order at the 2,000-meter checkpoint (Row 1) had no bearing on the scoring for Row 2.
Time cap: 2 hours for men, 2 hours 10 minutes for women.
Contested on Concept2 ergs inside the VELO Sports Center velodrome.
events.notes: The longest single effort in Games history at the time, keeping athletes on the erg for roughly 80 to 95 minutes. Time cap listed is the men's; women had 2 hours 10 minutes. Neal Maddox was 2nd for the men (1:19:25.9) and Justin Allen 3rd (1:19:39.7); Margaux Alvarez (1:29:02.2) and Ruth Anderson Horrell (1:29:18.4) followed Briggs for the women. Khalipa's double event win on the ergs vaulted him into early contention.

events.name: Burden Run
events.description:
For time:
Run 2.1 miles
Flip the Pig 100 yards (490-lb Pig men / 310-lb Pig women)
600-yard Log carry (100-lb log men / 70-lb log women)
Drag the Iditarod sled 66 yards (310-lb sled men / 220-lb sled women)
40-minute time cap.
Contested Friday morning (10:30 a.m. to 12:15 p.m.) on the track and in the soccer stadium. Implement weights were not printed on the official event card; they are as reported by Wikipedia.
events.notes: Games debut of the Pig, the giant steel-and-foam flipping box that became a recurring Games implement. With much lighter burdens, the women's winning time (28:03.9 by Ladeairous) was faster than the men's. Ben Smith was 2nd for the men (29:46.2) and Daniel Petro 3rd (29:53.0); Ruth Anderson Horrell was 2nd for the women (28:27.3) and Briggs 3rd (29:39.6). Khalipa's third straight event win.

events.name: ZigZag Sprint
events.description:
Sprint to the finish line 50 yards away, navigating around four padded obstacles (pylons).
4-round bracketed tournament contested Friday afternoon (1:00 to 2:45 p.m.) in the soccer stadium: six athletes raced head to head in each heat, with the top three finishers from each heat advancing to the next round. Places 1-6 were awarded to the athletes in the final round by finishing order; places 7-12 to third-round athletes by time; places 13-24 to second-round athletes by time; places 25 on to the remaining athletes by their first-round times.
events.notes: Pure head-to-head footspeed test, following 2012's straight-line sprint. Former Ohio State fullback Marcus Hendren beat Dan Bailey (2nd, by a margin officials measured to a thousandth of a second) and Aja Barto (3rd) in the men's final; per the games.crossfit.com recap 'Bracketology', Hendren's winning final time was 11.1 seconds, and his 10.9 in an earlier round was the fastest run of the day by any athlete. Michelle Crawford took the women's final over Lindy Wall (2nd) and Stacie Tovar (3rd); no time for the women's final was published, so her score stays as placement. Khalipa, the overall leader at the time, tied for 43rd. The official leaderboard records placement (e.g., '1 pt') rather than a time.

events.name: Legless
events.description:
For time:
27 Thrusters (95 lb men / 65 lb women)
4 Legless rope climbs
21 Thrusters (95 / 65 lb)
3 Legless rope climbs
15 Thrusters (95 / 65 lb)
2 Legless rope climbs
9 Thrusters (95 / 65 lb)
1 Legless rope climb
10-minute time cap.
Rope climbs to 15 feet performed without using the legs. Contested Friday night (6:00 to 8:50 p.m.) in the tennis stadium.
events.notes: Games debut of legless rope climbs (10 total), which shredded grip and biceps after a light 72-thruster engine test; many athletes hit the cap with climbs remaining and were scored with one second added per missed rep. Gary Helmick was 2nd for the men (6:08.1, eight tenths back) and Kenneth Leverich 3rd (6:17.6); Christy Phillips was 2nd for the women (9:41.9), with Valerie Voboril and Emily Carothers tied 3rd (10:02.0). Khalipa stalled on the ropes and finished 27th, opening the door for Froning.

events.name: Naughty Nancy
events.description:
Four rounds for time of:
Run 600 meters up and over the berm
25 Overhead squats (140 lb men / 95 lb women)
20-minute time cap.
Each 600-meter lap ran out of the soccer stadium and up and over a dirt berm before returning to the barbells on the field. Contested Saturday morning (8:00 to 9:50 a.m.).
events.notes: A supersized version of the benchmark 'Nancy' (normally 5 rounds of a 400-m run and 15 overhead squats at 95/65 lb): longer hill runs, bigger sets and heavier bars, 100 overhead squats in total. Bridges doubled up after his Legless win the night before; Froning was 2nd (17:19.3) and Khalipa 3rd (17:28.7). Briggs was 2nd for the women (17:27.7) and Voboril 3rd (17:50.2).

events.name: Clean & Jerk Ladder
events.description:
1-rep clean and jerk every 90 seconds with progressively heavier barbells.
Men's bars (lb): 225, 235, 245, 255, 265, 275, 285, 295, 305, 315, 325, 335, 345, 355, 365, 375, 385, 395, 405 (10-lb jumps).
Women's bars (lb): 145, 150, 155, 160, 165, 170, 175, 180, 185, 190, 195, 200, 205, 210, 215, 220, 225, 230, 235, 240, 245, 250 (5-lb jumps).
Four starting points (225 / 255 / 285 / 315 lb for men; 145 / 165 / 185 / 205 lb for women). Athletes were ranked by the weight of their heaviest successful lift, with partial credit awarded for a successful clean with a failed jerk (after at least one successful clean and jerk). An athlete who could not clean and jerk the opening weight was eliminated. Contested Saturday (11:45 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.) in the soccer stadium.
events.notes: Leaderboard decimals encode the partial-credit rule: x.20 means a completed clean and jerk at that weight, x.10 a clean only. Parker and Barto both clean-and-jerked 345 lb and cleaned 355 lb without the jerk to tie for first; Parker matched his C&J PR and set a new personal clean record. Froning jerked 345 lb (345.20, 3rd) to retake the overall lead while Khalipa missed at 335 lb and tied 7th. Games rookie Amanda Goodman, in last place overall entering the event, won the women's ladder with a 235-lb clean and jerk, a 10-lb PR; Lindsey Valenzuela and Elisabeth Akinwale tied 2nd at 235.10 (clean only). Nobody in either division finished the ladder (405 / 250 lb tops).

events.description:
For time:
Row 1,000 meters
Then, five rounds of:
25 Pull-ups
7 Push jerks (135 lb men / 85 lb women)
15-minute time cap.
A recreation of the final event of the inaugural 2007 CrossFit Games (125 pull-ups and 35 push jerks in total). Contested Saturday night (5:40 to 9:00 p.m.) in the tennis stadium.
events.notes: Throwback programming honoring the sport's roots; in 2007 the same workout (with a 1,000-m row on the ranch) decided the first Games. Bridges took his third event win of the weekend; Lacee Kovacs was 2nd (9:10.4) and Daniel Tyminski 3rd (9:12.5, tied with Daniel Petro on the leaderboard sort). For the women, Natalie McLain was 2nd (9:55.5) and Camille Leblanc-Bazinet 3rd (10:03.9).

events.name: Sprint Chipper
events.description:
For time:
21 Medicine-ball GHD sit-ups
15 Snatches (165 lb men / 100 lb women)
9 Wall burpees (burpees over a 6-foot wall)
5-minute time cap.
Contested Sunday (11:00 a.m. to 12:10 p.m.) in the soccer stadium. After this event the field was cut to the top 30 men and top 30 women, who advanced to the final two events.
events.notes: The GHD sit-ups were performed holding a medicine ball; the ball weight was not printed on the official card and is not stated in the games.crossfit.com event recap 'The Fast and the Fittest' either, so it is deliberately left unspecified rather than guessed. The recap confirms the workout as 21 med-ball GHD sit-ups, 15 snatches (165/100 lb) and 9 wall burpees with a 5-minute cap. The 6-foot wall height is per Wikipedia. Most athletes finished in around three minutes. In the women's final heat Jenn Jones cleared the wall first but tripped sprinting for the line, handing Briggs the event win by three tenths (2:35.3 to 2:35.6); Talayna Fortunato was 3rd (2:41.1). Dan Bailey was 2nd for the men (2:30.0) and ZA Anderson 3rd (2:33.6). The first of Froning's three straight event wins to close the Games.

events.name: The Cinco 1
events.description:
For time:
Three rounds of:
5 Deadlifts (405 lb men / 265 lb women)
5 Weighted one-legged squats, left leg (53-lb kettlebell men / 35-lb kettlebell women)
5 Weighted one-legged squats, right leg (53 / 35-lb kettlebell)
Then, 80-foot handstand walk
7-minute time cap. The Cinco 2 began precisely 1 minute after the time cap.
Contested Sunday afternoon (2:00 to 5:00 p.m.) in the tennis stadium by the top 30 men and top 30 women only.
events.notes: First of the back-to-back 'Cinco' finals (everything in fives), contested only by the post-cut top 30. Akinwale's 3:32.2 was the fastest time in either division. Ben Smith was 2nd for the men (4:17.3) and Scott Panchik 3rd (4:25.5); Talayna Fortunato was 2nd for the women (4:36.4) and Danielle Horan 3rd (4:46.6). Athletes still on the floor at the cap had one second added per uncompleted rep, then got one minute of rest before The Cinco 2.

events.name: The Cinco 2
events.description:
For time:
Three rounds of:
5 Muscle-ups
5 Deficit handstand push-ups
Then, 90-foot overhead walking lunge (160-lb axle bar men / 100-lb axle bar women)
7-minute time cap.
Began exactly 1 minute after the end of The Cinco 1's time cap, in the tennis stadium, contested by the top 30 men and top 30 women only. The handstand push-up deficit height was not printed on the official card; the games.crossfit.com retrospective 'How Two Handstand Push-ups Cost Alessandra Pichelli $65,000' describes the women's event as five nine-inch deficit handstand push-ups per round. No equivalent figure was found for the men's deficit.
events.notes: The title-deciding final event. Froning won it (his third straight event win) to finish on 962 points and claim his third consecutive championship; Josh Bridges was 2nd (5:40.8) and Khalipa 3rd (5:52.6). Fortunato edged Camille Leblanc-Bazinet by half a second (6:47.3 to 6:47.8) with Michele Letendre 3rd (7:01.0, a capped score under the plus-one-second-per-rep rule). The deficit handstand push-ups (9-inch deficit for the women, per the games.crossfit.com Pichelli retrospective) wrecked much of the women's final heat; per that article only Fortunato and Valenzuela got through them without trouble, and two missed reps at the cap cost Pichelli her hold on the overall podium. Briggs finished mid-pack but had already sealed the title (920 points); Valerie Voboril took 3rd overall on a tiebreaker over Alessandra Pichelli after both ended with 818 points.

years.formatNotes: Eighth CrossFit Games, third at the StubHub Center. Qualification ran through the worldwide Open (a record 209,585 registrants) and 17 Regionals. 43 men and 42 women started (the official leaderboard API lists totalCompetitors 43 for women, but Rory Long-Zambard appears unranked with an overall score of 0 and no score in any of the 13 events, confirming she did not start; the other 42 women all have recorded scores). 13 separately scored individual events: The Beach at Hermosa Beach Pier and a 1-rep-max overhead squat on Wednesday, July 23, then nothing Thursday (Masters and team day), three days of competition Friday through Sunday. Most events were worth up to 100 placement points; the two Sprint Sled races were worth 50 points each. All athletes competed through Event 11 (Midline March), after which only the top 30 men and top 30 women advanced to the final two tennis-stadium events, Thick 'n Quick and Double Grace, run back to back with 2 minutes between them. The Clean Speed Ladder introduced a new bracket format: quarterfinal (top 24 advance), semifinal (top 8 advance) and final, with athletes ranked by how far they advanced and their ladder time or heaviest clean. Wanda Brenton withdrew after Event 2, Albert-Dominic Larouche after Event 6, Pip Malone after Event 10, and Kara Webb and Nicole Holcomb after Event 11.
years.yearSummary: 2014 was the year Rich Froning was finally pushed deep into Sunday and still won, claiming a fourth consecutive title (925 points) over 24-year-old rookie Mat Fraser (875), with Jason Khalipa third. Camille Leblanc-Bazinet broke through for her first title (918) over Annie Thorisdottir, returning from a back injury year, with med-school student Julie Foucher third. The programming opened with the longest Games swim yet (1,000 yards of ocean at Hermosa Beach inside a triplet with kettlebell thrusters and sand burpees) and a spectator-friendly Wednesday-night 1-rep-max overhead squat, where Froning and Fraser tied at 377 lb. Friday's Triple 3 (3k row, 300 double-unders, 3-mile run) handed Froning a 37th-place finish, the worst of his Games career, before he stormed back to win five of the last eight events, including the famous Push Pull duel he narrowly lost to Josh Bridges and the surprise Double Grace finale he won. New tests included the aerodynamic Sprint Sled (two 50-point pure sprint races), kettlebell thrusters, the cylinder/sandbag Sprint Carry, and the bracket-style Clean Speed Ladder won by Neal Maddox and Elisabeth Akinwale. The field was cut to 30 after Midline March, keeping the late-weekend cut introduced in recent years.

events.name: The Beach
events.description:
For time:
Swim 250 yards
50 kettlebell thrusters (35 / 24 lb.)
30 burpees
Swim 500 yards
30 burpees
50 kettlebell thrusters (35 / 24 lb.)
Swim 250 yards
Contested Wednesday morning, July 23, in the ocean at the Hermosa Beach Pier. 1,000 total yards of open-water swimming around buoys, with the thrusters and burpees performed on the sand at the waterline. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Fourth straight year the Games opened in the water and the longest Games swim to date (1,000 yards, vs. 500 yards in the 2013 Pool, 700 m at 2012 Pendleton and 210 m at 2011 Santa Monica). Women's winner Anna Tunnicliffe (listed as Anna Tobias on the current leaderboard) is a 2008 Olympic sailing gold medalist. Rich Froning was 8th (35:10.11); Camille Leblanc-Bazinet 6th (35:58.54). Sources conflict on whether the thrusters used one or two kettlebells: Breaking Muscle's pre-event analysis described double-kettlebell thrusters, while the official card lists only '50 kettlebell thrusters (35 / 24 lb.)'.

events.name: Overhead Squat
events.description:
1-rep-max overhead squat.
Athletes each had 3 attempts to establish a maximum, choosing their own weights with increments as small as 1 lb.
Contested Wednesday evening, July 23, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points; scored by heaviest successful lift.
events.notes: First event announced for 2014 (revealed July 9, two weeks early). Froning and Fraser tied at 377 lb and both received the full 100 points. Kara Webb's (now Kara Saunders) 250 lb beat eventual champion Camille Leblanc-Bazinet's 242 lb by 8 lb. Wanda Brenton withdrew from the competition after this event.

events.name: Triple 3
events.description:
For time:
Row 3,000 meters
300 double-unders
Run 3 miles
Contested Friday morning, July 25, staged outside the track and soccer stadium; the 3-mile run looped around the StubHub Center grounds. Athletes competed in one large heat per division. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Rich Froning finished 37th (38:31.38), the worst Games event finish of his career to that point; he walked portions of the run. Triple 3 became a repeated Games test in later years. Australian Rob Forte and Norwegian Kristin Holte took the wins.

events.name: Sprint Sled 1
events.description:
Sled push for time (100 yards men / 60 yards women).
Athletes pushed the new aerodynamic Sprint Sled straight down the soccer-stadium field; the official card lists no sled weight.
Time cap: 2 minutes.
Contested Friday afternoon, July 25. Worth 50 points.
events.notes: The Sprint Sled was announced as the 'first piece of new equipment for 2014.' Sled weight is stored as null because sources conflict and the official card lists no weight: Wikipedia and WODwell list a 90-lb sled with 100/60-yard distances for men/women, the official pre-Games announcement said both events were '100-yard sled pushes,' and Rogue's equipment page describes the men's sled rigged with a 35-lb C-70 bar plus two 60-lb drums and the women's with a 25-lb C-63 bar plus two 45-lb drums. One of two 50-point events run back to back.

events.name: Sprint Sled 2
events.description:
Sled push for time (100 yards men / 60 yards women).
Same course and sled as Sprint Sled 1, contested as a second, separately scored effort shortly afterward.
Time cap: 3 minutes.
Contested Friday afternoon, July 25. Worth 50 points.
events.notes: Winning times more than doubled versus Sprint Sled 1 (Maddox :30.33 to 1:09.89) because the second race was run on already-fatigued legs minutes after the first; the time cap was extended from 2 to 3 minutes. Neal Maddox swept both sled events. The official card lists no equipment change between Sled 1 and Sled 2, and lists no sled weight; sled weight is stored as null because sources conflict (Wikipedia/WODwell say 90 lb for both divisions, while Rogue's equipment page describes differently rigged men's and women's sleds - see Sprint Sled 1 notes).

events.name: 21-15-9 Complex
events.description:
For time:
8 deadlifts (155 / 115 lb.)
7 cleans (155 / 115 lb.)
6 snatches (155 / 115 lb.)
8 pull-ups
7 chest-to-bar pull-ups
6 bar muscle-ups
6 deadlifts (155 / 115 lb.)
5 cleans (155 / 115 lb.)
4 snatches (155 / 115 lb.)
6 pull-ups
5 chest-to-bar pull-ups
4 bar muscle-ups
4 deadlifts (155 / 115 lb.)
3 cleans (155 / 115 lb.)
2 snatches (155 / 115 lb.)
4 pull-ups
3 chest-to-bar pull-ups
2 bar muscle-ups
Time cap: 7 minutes.
Each round totals 21, then 15, then 9 reps on both the barbell complex (deadlift/clean/snatch) and the pull-up bar complex (pull-up/chest-to-bar/bar muscle-up). Contested Friday evening, July 25, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Announced by Dave Castro the same day it was contested. The eventual champions, Froning and Leblanc-Bazinet, both won this event under the Friday-night lights. Albert-Dominic Larouche withdrew after this event.

events.name: Muscle-Up Biathlon
events.description:
For time:
400-meter run
18 muscle-ups
400-meter run
15 muscle-ups
400-meter run
12 muscle-ups
Penalty: each time the athlete breaks a set of muscle-ups, they must immediately run a 200-meter lap before resuming.
Time cap: 18 minutes.
Contested Saturday afternoon, July 26, in the soccer stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: Biathlon-style penalty-lap format. Rookie and former gymnast Cody Anderson famously went unbroken on all 45 ring muscle-ups to win; Froning finished 13th. Camille Leblanc-Bazinet was 2nd for the women (16:09.26) behind Tiffany Hendrickson.

events.name: Sprint Carry
events.description:
For time:
Sprint 100 yards
100-yard carry (100 / 60 lb. cylinder)
Sprint 100 yards
100-yard carry (120 / 80 lb. sandbag)
Sprint 100 yards
100-yard carry (150 / 100 lb. cylinder)
Down-and-back 100-yard shuttles across the soccer field: an unloaded sprint out, then carry an increasingly heavy object back, three times through.
Contested Saturday afternoon, July 26, in the soccer stadium. Worth 100 points.
events.notes: The pre-Games announcement listed the carries heaviest-first (150-lb cylinder, sandbag, 100-lb cylinder), but the event was contested with ascending loads as shown on the official workout archive and described by Wikipedia ('increasingly heavy objects'). Lauren Brooks doubled up after her Sprint Sled 1 win; Froning finished 15th.

events.name: Clean Speed Ladder
events.description:
Three-round elimination bracket; athletes ranked by their time to complete each ladder, or by the heaviest weight cleaned.
Quarterfinal round, for time:
1 squat clean (245 / 155 lb.)
1 squat clean (255 / 160 lb.)
1 squat clean (265 / 165 lb.)
1 squat clean (270 / 170 lb.)
1 squat clean (275 / 175 lb.)
Time cap: 2 minutes. Top 24 athletes advance.
Semifinal round, for time:
1 squat clean (280 / 180 lb.)
1 squat clean (290 / 185 lb.)
1 squat clean (300 / 190 lb.)
1 squat clean (305 / 195 lb.)
1 squat clean (310 / 200 lb.)
Time cap: 3 minutes. Top 8 athletes advance.
Final round, for time:
1 squat clean (315 / 205 lb.)
1 squat clean (325 / 210 lb.)
1 squat clean (335 / 215 lb.)
1 squat clean (340 / 220 lb.)
1 squat clean (345 / 225 lb.)
Time cap: 4 minutes.
Contested Saturday evening, July 26, in the tennis stadium. Worth 100 points.
