The individual field was cut once mid-competition: after Saturday's events it was reduced from 40 to 30 athletes for the Sunday final day (the only mid-competition cut of the week; per the official announcement games.crossfit.com/announcement/13704), so the three Sunday events (11/The Alpaca, 12/Back Nine, 13/Jackie Pro) were scored on a 30-athlete points table. The 2022 NOBULL CrossFit Games were Adrian Bozman's first as Director of Competition after Dave Castro's removal. Thirteen named tests produced FOURTEEN scored events: Shuttle to Overhead was scored as two separate 100-point events (2A = total running time, 2B = total jerks), so the official event numbering runs 1, 2A, 2B, 3-13 and the maximum possible score was 1,400 points on the standard 100-point Games table. Severe storms on Wednesday, Aug. 3 forced an evacuation of the outdoor venues and pushed Shuttle to Overhead from Wednesday afternoon to Thursday, so the chronological order of contest differs from the official event numbers (Events 3 and 4 were contested Wednesday night before Event 2). Rain on the final morning also forced the legless rope climbs to be cut from The Alpaca. Justin Medeiros (1,184 points) repeated without winning a single event, the first male champion to do so since 2007, ahead of Roman Khrennikov (1,157) and Ricky Garard (1,068). Tia-Clair Toomey (1,158) won a record sixth consecutive title ahead of 18-year-old Mal O'Brien (1,045), the youngest individual podium finisher ever, and Laura Horvath (981).
years.yearSummary: Adrian Bozman's first Games as competition director leaned hard into novelty and strongman flavor: pig flips, a 1-rep-max sandbag-to-shoulder ladder, jerry-bag and Husafell carries, a kettlebell-loaded sled, parallel-bar traverse dips, block deficit handstand push-ups, and the brutal double-under crossovers that wrecked the Skill Speed Medley final all appeared, and The Capitol sent athletes on a point-to-point road race that finished on the steps of the Wisconsin State Capitol. Weather repeatedly intervened, postponing Shuttle to Overhead by a day and stripping the rope climbs out of The Alpaca. Justin Medeiros defended his title on pure consistency, becoming the first men's champion since James FitzGerald in 2007 to win without taking a single event, while Roman Khrennikov, finally able to enter the U.S., pushed him to the final day. Tia-Clair Toomey claimed a record sixth straight title, with teenage phenom Mal O'Brien second and Laura Horvath winning back-to-back events on the final day to grab third. Nick Mathew and Emma Lawson were named the Games' first co-Rookies of the Year.

events.name: Bike to Work
events.description:
For time:
75 toes-to-bars
5-mile bike (5 laps of a 1-mile course)
75 chest-to-bar pull-ups
5-mile bike (5 laps of a 1-mile course)

The bike course looped around the North Park grounds over grass, gravel, and concrete sections.
Time cap: 50 minutes.
events.notes: Opening event of the Games, contested at North Park before storms shut down the outdoor venues for the afternoon. Haley Adams took her first career Games event win, edging Tia-Clair Toomey by about 3 seconds; Jonne Koski was second to Garard by under 2 seconds in the men's race.

events.name: Skill Speed Medley
events.description:
Three-round elimination race, 3-minute cap per round (3-3-3 minutes on the official card).

Opening round (all 40 athletes, in heats):
3 pegboard ascents (men) / 2 pegboard ascents (women)
75 unbroken single-unders
10 unbroken single-leg squats, left leg
10 unbroken single-leg squats, right leg
Handstand-walk obstacle course
Top 20 advance.

Semifinal round:
2 strict pegboard ascents (men) / 1 strict pegboard ascent (women)
50 unbroken double-unders
10 unbroken single-leg squats, left leg
10 unbroken single-leg squats, right leg
Handstand-walk obstacle course with pirouette start
Top 5 advance.

Final round:
1 strict pegboard ascent
25 double-under crossovers
10 unbroken single-leg squats, left leg
10 unbroken single-leg squats, right leg
Handstand-walk obstacle course with low start

Final placement determined overall event ranking (placement points).
events.notes: timeCapMin is the 9-minute total of the three round caps (3-3-3 minutes per round on the official card); rounds were separately clocked elimination heats, each an under-3-minute sprint effort. Contested Wednesday night in the Coliseum as official Event 3, before Event 2 (Shuttle to Overhead), which the storms had pushed to Thursday. The double-under crossovers in the final proved disastrous for most finalists: only two men completed the final-round course, and no woman got through the closing movements; Danielle Brandon won the women's final on furthest progression.

events.name: Elizabeth Elevated
events.description:
21-15-9-9-9 reps for time of:
Squat cleans (135 lb men / 95 lb women)
Dips, with parallel-bar traverses

Each round's dips had to be split into 3 unbroken sets, each set beginning with a traverse down the parallel bars (round of 21 = traverse + 7 dips, three times; round of 15 = 3 x 5; rounds of 9 = 3 x 3).
Time cap: 10 minutes men / 12 minutes women.
events.notes: A twist on the classic benchmark Elizabeth (21-15-9 squat cleans and ring dips), swapping ring dips for parallel-bar dips broken up by bar traverses and extending the rep scheme. Time cap differed by division (men 10:00, women 12:00). Arielle Loewen took her first career Games event win. Closed out day 1 in the Coliseum.

events.name: Shuttle to Overhead A
events.description:
On a 12-minute running clock, three rounds of shuttle runs plus max jerks (300 lb men / 200 lb women):
0:00-2:00 - 400-m shuttle run, then max jerks in the remaining time
Rest 1 minute
3:00-6:00 - 600-m shuttle run, then max jerks in the remaining time
Rest 2 minutes
8:00-12:00 - 800-m shuttle run, then max jerks in the remaining time

Scored as two separate 100-point events. Event 2A score: the sum of the three shuttle-run times.
events.notes: Originally scheduled for Wednesday afternoon; severe storms forced an evacuation of North Park and moved the event to Thursday, Aug. 4, the individuals' only test that day. One test, two scores: 2A ranked total running time, 2B (separate entry) ranked total jerks. Haley Adams won her second running-based score of the Games.

events.name: Shuttle to Overhead B
events.description:
Same test as Shuttle to Overhead A (one 12-minute running clock):
0:00-2:00 - 400-m shuttle run, then max jerks (300 lb men / 200 lb women)
Rest 1 minute
3:00-6:00 - 600-m shuttle run, then max jerks
Rest 2 minutes
8:00-12:00 - 800-m shuttle run, then max jerks

Event 2B score: total jerks completed across all three rounds.
events.notes: The faster the runs, the more time remained to accumulate jerks at a very heavy load (300/200 lb); the barbell was pre-loaded at the jerk station so athletes did not have to clean it from the floor each round (setup detail reported from broadcast, not on the official card). Adler's 19 reps at 300 lb and Toomey's 18 at 200 lb won the B scores.

events.name: The Capitol
events.description:
For time, point to point:
20 Pig flips (510-lb Pig men / 350-lb Pig women)
Run approx. 3.5 miles from North Park through downtown Madison
200-m jerry-bag carry (two 100-lb bags men / two 70-lb bags women)
200-m Husafell-bag carry (200 lb men / 150 lb women)

Finish at the steps of the Wisconsin State Capitol. No time cap.
events.notes: Point-to-point road event starting at North Park on the Alliant Energy Center campus and finishing on the Wisconsin State Capitol steps, with spectators lining the route through downtown Madison. Garard's second event win of the Games; Migała's win was her first of the week.

events.name: Up and Over
events.description:
3 rounds for time of:
12 muscle-ups
25 jump-overs (the obstacle changes each round: 50-in log; 42-in box men / 30-in box women; 20-in Pig)
30 GHD sit-ups

Then:
84-ft weighted walking lunge with an axle bar (185 lb men / 125 lb women)

Hands were not allowed on the boxes for the jump-overs.
Time cap: 18 minutes.
events.notes: The official card lists simply 'muscle-ups' (36 total); the event was contested on rings at North Park per broadcast footage, but no written source specifies ring vs. bar, so treat that detail with caution. The no-hands rule on the 42/30-in box jump-overs proved much harder than expected. Saxon Panchik led wire to wire for his second career event win; Toomey's win was the 35th Games event win of her career and extended her overall lead.

events.name: Echo Press
events.description:
For time:
30-cal Echo bike (men) / 25-cal (women)
10 block handstand push-ups
20-cal Echo bike (men) / 15-cal (women)
10 block handstand push-ups
20-cal Echo bike (men) / 15-cal (women)
10 block handstand push-ups
30-cal Echo bike (men) / 25-cal (women)

The handstand push-ups were performed on raised blocks: athletes walked up the wall onto the block, lowered the head below the level of the block (3.5-in deficit men / 2-in deficit women), and pressed back to a handstand.
Time cap: 10 minutes men / 12 minutes women.
events.notes: Friday night in the Coliseum (100 total calories for men, 80 for women, plus 30 block HSPUs). The block setup for the handstand push-ups was a new Games implement. First career event wins for both Will Moorad and Alexis Raptis. Ricky Garard struggled badly here, beginning his slide from the overall lead.

events.name: Rinse 'N' Repeat
events.description:
8 rounds, every 2 minutes:
50-yd swim (25 yd down and back)
SkiErg calories

Rounds 1-6: the required SkiErg calories increase each round - 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. Athletes who fail to finish the swim and the required calories inside the 2-minute window are eliminated.
Rounds 7-8: athletes who complete round 6 swim, then accumulate max calories in the remaining time.

Score: total calories completed.
events.notes: Held off campus at the Soderholm Family Aquatic Center pool (Nicholas Recreation Center, University of Wisconsin-Madison). Rounds 1-6 totaled 78 fixed calories; the winners added 82 (Khrennikov) and 59 (Campbell) in the two max-effort rounds. Former competitive swimmer Lucy Campbell took her first Games event win; Khrennikov's win was his first ever at the Games.

events.name: Hat Trick
events.description:
3 rounds, each for time, of:
Sprint (down the North Park floor)
20 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball to 12-ft target men / 14-lb ball to 11-ft target women)
6 dumbbell snatches (100 lb men / 70 lb women, alternating arms each rep)

Time cap: 2 minutes per round. Rest 4 minutes between rounds (two heats alternated on the floor during the rest windows).
Score: sum of the three round times.
events.notes: timeCapMin is the 14-minute overall window (3 x 2:00 work intervals, each round capped at 2:00, with 4 minutes rest between rounds). The sprint distance was never published on the official card. First career Games event wins for Guilherme Malheiros and Ellie Turner. Justin Medeiros moved into the overall lead after this event, overtaking Ricky Garard, and never relinquished it.

events.name: Sandbag Ladder
events.description:
1-rep-max sandbag-to-shoulder.

Athletes worked through a ladder of progressively heavier sandbags, from 240 lb up to 340 lb (men) and 160 lb up to 250 lb (women), with 2 attempts per bag. A successful rep required getting the bag to one shoulder, stabilizing it, and extending the free arm to show control.

Athletes who failed (or topped out) at the same bag were separated by a tiebreak race: 3 progressively heavier sandbags (100, 150, 200 lb men / 50, 100, 150 lb women) lifted over a yoke crossbar for time.
events.notes: Four men (Malheiros, Mathew, Fikowski, Hopper) shouldered the heaviest 340-lb bag, so organizers rolled out a surprise bag listed around 350 lb; nobody lifted it and all four went to the tiebreak, where Malheiros and Mathew clocked identical times and shared the event win. Speegle was the only woman to shoulder the 250-lb bag. Medeiros topped out at 330 lb. Exact intermediate bag weights in the ladder were not published.

events.name: The Alpaca
events.description:
For time (as published):
126-ft sled push, decreasing in load (sled starts loaded with all 6 kettlebells; pairs are unloaded along the way)
2 legless rope climbs
20 kettlebell clean and jerks
42-ft sled push with 2 kettlebells
2 legless rope climbs
15 kettlebell clean and jerks
42-ft sled push with 4 kettlebells
2 legless rope climbs
10 kettlebell clean and jerks
42-ft sled push with 6 kettlebells

Kettlebells: six 32-kg bells (men) / six 24-kg bells (women); clean and jerks performed with a pair.
Time cap: 18 minutes.

As contested: overnight rain left the ropes unsafe, and all legless rope climbs were removed from the event on the morning of competition.
events.notes: The published workout included 6 legless rope climbs, but they were cut due to wet ropes from weather, turning the test into a sled-push/kettlebell couplet (movements listed as contested; winning times reflect the modified event). Khrennikov's second event win of the Games kept his title challenge alive; Horvath began her back-to-back final-day wins.

events.name: Back Nine
events.description:
For time:
54-ft yoke carry (665 lb men / 485 lb women)
2 front squats (315 lb men / 215 lb women)
3 deadlifts (475 lb men / 315 lb women)
2 front squats (315 lb men / 215 lb women)
54-ft yoke carry (665 lb men / 485 lb women)

Barbell work from the floor.
Time cap: 4 minutes.
events.notes: Featured the heaviest yoke (665 lb) and heaviest deadlift (475 lb) programmed at the Games to that point. Horvath won her second straight event of the final day; Adler took his second score win of the week (after Shuttle to Overhead B).

events.name: Jackie Pro
events.description:
For time:
1,000-m row
50 thrusters (95 lb men / 65 lb women)
30 bar muscle-ups

The 1,000-m row had to be completed in under 3:15 (men) / 3:40 (women).
Time cap: 10 minutes men / 11 minutes women.
events.notes: Final event of the Games, a heavier-skill 'pro' version of the benchmark Jackie (1,000-m row, 50 x 45/35-lb thrusters, 30 pull-ups) with Jackie's pull-ups upgraded to bar muscle-ups. Time cap differed by division (men 10:00, women 11:00). Lucy Campbell won her second event of the weekend; Medeiros and Toomey crossed as champions moments later.

years.formatNotes: 40 men and 40 women qualified through the Open, Quarterfinals, and Semifinals. Twelve tests over four days of individual competition (Thursday Aug 3 - Sunday Aug 6), three per day. Mid-competition cuts returned: the field was cut from 40 to 30 after Friday's Test 6 and from 30 to 20 after Saturday's Test 9. Standard 100-point Games scoring table (100 points per event win), maximum 1,200 points. Final year with NOBULL as title sponsor. Jeffrey Adler (953) won ahead of Patrick Vellner (837) and Roman Khrennikov (801); Laura Horvath (966) won ahead of Emma Lawson (919) and Arielle Loewen (883).
years.yearSummary: Adrian Bozman's second Games as competition director opened with a 40-minute mountain-bike race and closed with a barbell-and-bike sprint in North Park, with no swim event for the first time in years. The programming leaned on heavy odd objects (a 510-lb Pig, the heaviest implement in Games history, kettlebell-loaded sleds, sandbag squats and sandbag-over-log carries) and high gymnastics skill (free-standing handstand push-ups, pirouette obstacles, pull-overs, parallel-bar traverses, heavy-rope double-unders), plus a pure Olympic Total contested Saturday night in the Coliseum. With six-time champion Tia-Clair Toomey absent on maternity, Laura Horvath finally broke through for Hungary's first title with five event wins, including three straight to open the final stretch (Olympic Total, Muscle-Up Logs, Parallel-Bar Pull). Jeffrey Adler became the first Canadian man to win the Games, overtaking Roman Khrennikov on the final day after Khrennikov broke his foot during the Parallel-Bar Pull and gutted out the final event on one leg to hold a podium spot. Mid-competition cuts (40 to 30 to 20) returned after a year without them.

events.name: Ride
events.description:
As many laps as possible in 40 minutes on a Trek Marlin 8 mountain bike.

Off-road lap course built on the Alliant Energy Center grounds; each lap was approximately 2,400 m of riding plus a short run with the bike back to the remount point (sources report the run segment as 80-200 m, for a total lap of roughly 2,600 m).

Score: laps completed in 40 minutes; ties on laps were separated by finish time of the final lap.
events.notes: First individual test of the Games, ridden on Trek Marlin 8 mountain bikes supplied by Trek (headquartered in nearby Waterloo, WI). Large lead groups finished on the same lap count (10 men and 10 women logged 7 laps), so placements within a lap count came down to finishing time; Jonne Koski and Emma Lawson took the wins. Sources differ on the exact length of the per-lap run segment (80 m vs 200 m). Note: Breaking Muscle's day-one results article listed Ant Haynes as the men's Event 1 leader, but the official games.crossfit.com leaderboard (division=1, sort=1) confirms Jonne Koski at rank 1 with 7 laps / 100 pts; the Breaking Muscle table is the outlier and its day-one article was dropped as a source for this event.

events.name: Pig Chipper
events.description:
For time:
10 Pig flips (510-lb Pig M / 350-lb Pig W)
25 chest-to-bar pull-ups
50 toes-to-bars
100 wall-ball shots (20-lb ball to 10-ft target M / 14-lb ball to 9-ft target W)
50 toes-to-bars
25 chest-to-bar pull-ups
10 Pig flips

Time cap: 18 minutes.
events.notes: The men's 510-lb Pig was reported as the heaviest implement ever used at the CrossFit Games. The Pig itself had appeared at the Games before (including 2022), so it was not a debut implement. Laura Horvath's 13:50.40 was faster than the men's winning time.

events.name: Inverted Medley
events.description:
For time:
30-ft unbroken handstand walk over the ramp
8 free-standing handstand push-ups
Unbroken obstacle steps to a 180-degree pirouette
16 pull-overs
Unbroken obstacle steps to a 360-degree pirouette
8 free-standing handstand push-ups
30-ft unbroken handstand walk over the ramp

Time cap: 7 minutes.
events.notes: Pure gymnastics-skill test contested Thursday night in the Coliseum. The handstand walk over the ramp and the obstacle-step segments had to be unbroken. Free-standing handstand push-ups returned after debuting at the 2021 Games; the obstacle-step pirouettes (180 and 360 degrees) were new programming. Rookie handstand specialist Cole Greashaber took the men's win; Danielle Brandon dominated the women's field by 34 seconds.

events.name: The Alpaca Redux
events.description:
For time:
126-ft sled push, starting with all six kettlebells loaded (546 lb total M / 443 lb total W)
Then 3 rounds of:
2 legless rope climbs
12 kettlebell clean and jerks (two 70-lb kettlebells M / two 53-lb kettlebells W)
42-ft sled push (sled starts round 1 with two kettlebells; two kettlebells are added each round)

Time cap: 18 minutes.
events.notes: A redux of 2022's 'The Alpaca' kettlebell-sled test, this time WITH the legless rope climbs that rain forced out of the 2022 version. Many women finished at or near the time cap (winner Emma Tall came in under it at 15:54.01; overall champion Laura Horvath was capped). Khrennikov took his second event win of the week.

events.name: Ski-Bag
events.description:
For time:
30-calorie SkiErg
30 sandbag squats (200 lb M / 125 lb W)
20-calorie SkiErg
20 sandbag squats

Time cap: 6 minutes.
events.notes: Short heavy sprint couplet: the sandbag was held in the front-carry (bear-hug) position for the squats. Farm-strong Colten Mertens took his first career Games event win; Horvath grabbed her second win of the week.

events.name: Helena
events.description:
3 rounds for time:
400-m run
12 bar muscle-ups
21 dumbbell snatches (50 lb M / 35 lb W)

Time cap: 11 minutes.
events.notes: A skill-elevated nod to the classic benchmark Helen (run/kettlebell swings/pull-ups), swapping in bar muscle-ups and dumbbell snatches. Last event before the first cut (40 to 30). Eventual champion Jeffrey Adler took the men's win; Jamie Simmonds won her first event since returning from injury.

events.name: Cross-Country 5K
events.description:
For time:
Run 5 km on a cross-country course laid out around the Alliant Energy Center grounds.

Time cap: 30 minutes.
events.notes: Unloaded cross-country run to open Saturday. Belgian rookie Jelle Hoste won the men's race; Canada's Emily Rolfe won the women's.

events.name: Intervals
events.description:
2 intervals for total working time, on a 12-minute clock:

Interval 1 (begins at 0:00):
21 box jump-overs (24-in box M / 20-in box W, step-down)
15-calorie row
9 burpee box jump-overs (48-in box M / 36-in box W)
Rest until the 6:00 mark.

Interval 2 (begins at 6:00), reverse order:
9 burpee box jump-overs (48-in M / 36-in W)
15-calorie row
21 box jump-overs (24-in M / 20-in W, step-down)

Score: sum of the two interval times. Time cap: 12 minutes.
events.notes: The burpee box jump-overs used an unusually tall 48-in (M) / 36-in (W) box, while the standard box jump-overs used 24/20-in boxes with a required step-down. Second interval ran the triplet in reverse order.

events.name: Olympic Total
events.description:
For load:
1-rep-max snatch
1-rep-max clean and jerk

Each athlete received two 20-second lifting windows per lift (four windows total) to record their heaviest successful snatch and clean and jerk. Fractional plates allowed loading in 1-lb increments.

Score: best snatch + best clean and jerk.
events.notes: Contested Saturday night in the Coliseum, the last event before the cut to 20. Canadian rookie Jack Farlow won with a 305-lb snatch and a 396-lb clean and jerk for a 701-lb total, the only athlete over 700 lb; the 396-lb clean and jerk was reported as a men's live-competition Games-season record. Laura Horvath won the women's event with a 205-lb snatch and 265-lb clean and jerk (470 lb), the first of three consecutive event wins.

events.name: Muscle-up Logs
events.description:
5 rounds for time:
7 ring muscle-ups
1 sandbag carried over 3 logs (progressively taller logs, reported at approximately 4 ft, 5 ft, and 5 ft 5 in)

Sandbag: 150 lb M / 100 lb W in rounds 1-4; 200 lb M / 125 lb W in round 5.

Time cap: 13 minutes.
events.notes: Sunday opener in North Park. Adler's win here moved him past Khrennikov into the overall lead he never relinquished; Horvath's win was her second straight. Log heights are as reported by Breaking Muscle; the official card did not publish them.

events.name: Parallel-Bar Pull
events.description:
8 rounds for time:
Down-and-back parallel-bar (P-bar) traverse
30 heavy-rope double-unders
1 section hand-over-hand sled pull (345 lb M / 290 lb W)

Time cap: 15 minutes.
events.notes: Penultimate test, all upper-body pulling and skill; parallel bars returned after their 2022 Games debut, and the heavy (drag) rope double-unders were widely covered as a new Games movement, though no official source confirms a debut. Roman Khrennikov, sitting second overall, broke his foot during this event, finished last in it, and dropped behind Vellner; he still started the final event on the broken foot to protect the podium. Brent Fikowski's win was the 10th Games event win of his career; Horvath made it three in a row.

events.name: Echo Thruster Final
events.description:
For time:
21-calorie Echo Bike, then 21 thrusters (115 lb M / 85 lb W)
18-calorie Echo Bike, then 18 thrusters (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
15-calorie Echo Bike, then 15 thrusters (155 lb M / 105 lb W)
Then: 66-ft overhead walking lunge (155 lb M / 105 lb W)

Time cap: 10 minutes.
events.notes: Final event in North Park with ascending thruster loads and a 66-ft overhead lunge finisher. Dallin Pepper won the men's heat; 18-year-old rookie Olivia Kerstetter won the women's. Jeffrey Adler sealed the men's title (first Canadian man to win the Games) and Laura Horvath the women's; Roman Khrennikov completed the event on a broken foot to finish third overall.

years.formatNotes: 40 men and 40 women qualified via Open > Quarterfinals > Semifinals. Each event was worth a maximum of 100 points. The competition was profoundly altered on Day 1: Serbian athlete Lazar Dukic died during the swim portion of Event 1 (Lake Day), and the two remaining Day 1 events - 'Hammer Down' (4 rounds for time: 50 sledgehammer strikes with a 20/16-lb sledgehammer, 14 sandbag throws over a tire at 100/70 lb, 5 tire flips at 242 lb) and 'Amanda .45' (13-11-9-7-5 reps of muscle-ups and squat snatches, 12-minute cap) - were cancelled. Competition was paused and resumed Friday afternoon after consultation with athletes and the Dukic family. Roughly 13-16 athletes per the various reports withdrew in the following days, including reigning champions Laura Horvath and Jeffrey Adler, Lazar's brother Luka Dukic, Karin Freyova, Emma Tall, Elisa Fuliano, Victoria Campos, Sam Cournoyer, Guilherme Malheiros, Moritz Fiebig, Jacqueline Dahlstrom, Dani Speegle, and Arielle Loewen. The originally planned two cuts (to 30 after the Saturday morning event, to 20 by end of Saturday) were replaced with a single cut: the top 30 men and women after Saturday advanced to Sunday. 10 of the originally programmed 12 events were contested; events here are numbered 1-10 as actually contested (in original programming Chad was Event 7 and the Clean Ladder Event 8).
years.yearSummary: The 2024 Games in Fort Worth were defined by tragedy: Lazar Dukic drowned during the opening Lake Day swim-run, the rest of Day 1 was cancelled, and the event continued only after consultation with athletes and his family, with many competitors withdrawing in solidarity. The 10 contested events were a compressed version of the planned 12-event program, anchored indoors at Dickies Arena with offsite tests at Marine Creek Lake and Farrington Field. Programming spanned a 67-minute hero-workout grind (Chad 1000X, making its Games debut), an elimination-style clean ladder topping out at 365/250 lb, and back-to-back separately scored sprint finals with yoke carries. Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr, returning after the birth of her first child, won six of ten events and claimed a record-extending seventh title, while 22-year-old James Sprague emerged from a wide-open men's race - following the withdrawal of defending champion Jeffrey Adler - for his first title.

events.name: Lake Day
events.description:
For time:
3.5-mile run
800-meter open-water swim

Contested offsite at Marine Creek Lake, Fort Worth. Athletes completed the run first, then finished with the 800-m swim.
events.notes: Serbian athlete Lazar Dukic died during the swim portion of this event; his body was recovered later that day. The remaining two Day 1 events (Hammer Down and Amanda .45) were cancelled and the competition was paused until Friday afternoon. Victor Hoffer is recorded as withdrawn during the event. The tragedy prompted widespread scrutiny of event safety and water-rescue provisioning.

events.name: Midline Climb
events.description:
For time:
50 deadlifts (225 lb M / 155 lb W)
3 rope climbs
50/30-cal ski erg (M/W)
3 rope climbs
50 GHD sit-ups
3 rope climbs

3 rope climbs

3 rope climbs
50 deadlifts (225 lb M / 155 lb W)

Time cap: 20 minutes
events.notes: First event after competition resumed following Lazar Dukic's death; coverage described a restrained, respectful atmosphere as athletes returned. Source conflict: the official games.crossfit.com workout page and WODconnect list 3 rope climbs at each of the 5 rope stations (15 total); the Wikipedia event table summary lists 5 per station. Recorded as 3 per the official source.

events.name: Firestorm
events.description:
3 rounds for time:
15/11-cal Echo bike (M/W)
11 burpees over barricade

Time cap: 4 minutes (men) / 5 minutes (women)
events.notes: Time caps differed by gender: 4:00 for men, 5:00 for women (BarBend: 'aggressive time cap of five minutes for the women and four for the men'). The schema's single timeCapMin field cannot hold both, so it records the larger women's cap (5); the men's 4:00 cap is in the description. Australian Grace Walton took the women's event win.

events.name: Track and Field
events.description:
Two separately timed parts, one event score (combined placement across the parts). Contested Friday night offsite at Farrington Field.

Part 1 - For time:
1,600-meter run

Part 2 - begins at the 12:00 mark - For time:
50-yard sprint
50-yard sandbag carry (100 lb M / 70 lb W)
75-yard sprint
75-yard sandbag carry (100 lb M / 70 lb W)
100-yard sprint

Time cap: none on Part 1 (12-minute window before Part 2); 3 minutes on Part 2.
events.notes: Scored on combined rank of the two parts, so no single winning time exists; Garard and Toomey-Orr each won both parts outright. Fastest sprint-course (Part 2) times: Garard 1:04.89, Toomey-Orr 1:13.10; fastest 1,600-m times: Garard 4:55.13, Toomey-Orr 5:30.16. Contested under lights at Farrington Field in roughly 88 F heat. Event podiums: men Garard, Luke Parker, Roman Khrennikov; women Toomey-Orr, Haley Adams, Aimee Cringle.

events.name: Chad
events.description:
For time:
1,000 weighted box step-ups wearing a ruck (45 lb M / 35 lb W), 20-inch box
*Completed as 250 trips (4 step-ups per trip) along rows of boxes on the arena floor.

Time cap: 67 minutes

Run as one single mixed heat: all remaining men and women (32 men, 35 women) on the floor together at Dickies Arena on Saturday morning.
events.notes: First time the hero benchmark Chad 1000X was contested at the Games, honoring Navy SEAL Senior Chief Chad Wilkinson and raising awareness of veteran suicide. The official card reads only '1,000 step-ups (35/45 lb), completed as 250 trips'; the 20-inch box is the benchmark standard and reported by BarBend, with each trip counted as 4 reps across rows of boxes. This was Sprague's first individual Games event win and a springboard to his title.

events.name: Clean Ladder
events.description:
Elimination-style power clean ladder, three rounds, each round for time (2-minute working window per round).

Round 1 (all remaining athletes, ~30): 5 bars, reps 3-3-2-2-1
Men 255-265-275-285-295 lb / Women 165-175-185-195-205 lb
Top 20 advance.

Round 2 (20 athletes): 4 bars, reps 2-1-1-1
Men 295-305-315-325 lb / Women 205-215-225-230 lb
Top 10 advance.

Round 3 (10 athletes): 3 bars, reps 1-1-1
Men 325-345-365 lb / Women 230-240-250 lb

Final placement by round reached, then completion/time within the round.
events.notes: Medeiros was first to clean the 365-lb final bar (37.24), edging Bruno Marins (37.74) and Travis Mayer. Toomey-Orr won the women's final round at 250 lb in 25.05 over Kyra Milligan (25.15). The 30/20/10 advancement reflects the published structure; exact Round 1 athlete counts varied slightly due to withdrawals. Rounds were separately clocked with a 2-minute working window each; timeCapMin (6) is the sum of the three per-round caps per the schema convention.

events.name: Push Pull 2.0
events.description:
For time:
45 handstand push-ups
80-foot sled pull, standing (180 lb M / 110 lb W)
30 strict handstand push-ups
80-foot seated sled pull (from the platform)
15 freestanding handstand push-ups (advancing every 3 reps)

Time cap: 10 minutes
events.notes: Sequel to the 2014 'Push Pull' event. Rookie Lexi Neely won the women's field by 28 seconds, finishing the 15 freestanding handstand push-ups in two sets. Minor source conflict on Panchik's time: BarBend and The Barbell Spin list 6:20.80, FitnessVolt 6:31.80; recorded 6:20.80. The cut to the top 30 for Sunday was applied after this event.

events.name: Dickies Triplet
events.description:
5 rounds for time:
175-meter run
12 toes-to-bars
8 alternating dumbbell snatches (100 lb M / 70 lb W)

Time cap: 11 minutes
events.notes: Opening event of the final day, contested by the top 30 (less withdrawals) inside Dickies Arena, with the run laps weaving through the arena. Hopper's second event win of the week.

events.name: Final 2421
events.description:
For time:
24 thrusters (95 lb M / 65 lb W)
24 chest-to-bar pull-ups
80-foot yoke carry (425 lb M / 245 lb W)
21 chest-to-bar pull-ups
21 thrusters (95 lb M / 65 lb W)

Time cap: 5 minutes

Followed by 2 minutes rest, then Final 1815 (separately scored).
events.notes: First half of the back-to-back GORUCK finals, each scored as its own 100-point event with 2 minutes rest between.

events.name: Final 1815
events.description:
For time (begins 2 minutes after completion of Final 2421):
18 thrusters (135 lb M / 95 lb W)
18 bar muscle-ups
80-foot yoke carry (525 lb M / 345 lb W)
15 bar muscle-ups
15 thrusters (135 lb M / 95 lb W)

Time cap: 7 minutes
events.notes: Hatfield swept both finals; Toomey-Orr's win sealed her record seventh title (951 points) while James Sprague (806) held off Dallin Pepper (785) and Brent Fikowski (765) for his first. Minor source conflict: The Barbell Spin lists Toomey-Orr at 4:40; BarBend and FitnessVolt list 4:33.89, recorded here.

years.formatNotes: Sharply reduced format: 30 men and 30 women (down from 40), 10 events over 3 days (down from 4), no cuts. Quarterfinals were eliminated from the season, so athletes qualified through the Open and in-person Semifinals. Standard 100-point Games table per event for a 1,000-point maximum. The men's race was the closest podium finish in Games history: Jayson Hopper (787) over Ricky Garard (773) and James Sprague (772), decided on the final event. Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr (902) won her eighth title ahead of Lucy Campbell (720) and Olivia Kerstetter (678). The Games moved to Albany's MVP Arena after two years in Fort Worth, amid a season of athlete-safety fallout from the 2024 Games (Open registration fell 32% to 233,815) and the absence of several stars from the field.
years.yearSummary: The first Games in Albany were deliberately stripped down: three days, ten events, thirty athletes per division, and a return to classic CrossFit tests rather than spectacle. Programming opened with a long offsite run/row/run on the Hudson riverfront, then leaned on arena staples - wall walks and crossovers, a pegboard/squat-clean ladder, heavy axle deadlifts with handstand walks, a back-to-back ski/bike sprint pair, and a yoke-and-deficit-HSPU grinder - plus the first standalone 1RM back squat event in Games history, where Colten Mertens' 570-lb squat broke an 18-year-old Games record. Jayson Hopper survived two late no-reps in Running Isabel to claim his first title in the closest men's podium race ever contested, with Ricky Garard edging James Sprague by a single point for second. Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr was dominant in her eighth championship, winning four of ten events, while Britain's Lucy Campbell broke out with two event wins and second overall.

events.name: Run/Row/Run
events.description:
For time:
4-mile run
3,000-meter row
2-mile run

Contested offsite at Jennings Landing on the Hudson riverfront in downtown Albany; Concept2 rowers were staged at the landing between the two run legs. No loads. No published time cap.
events.notes: Opening event, free to spectate, with a community division running scaled versions alongside the pros. 2023 champion Jeffrey Adler won the men's race by 10 seconds over Roman Khrennikov (46:26), with Ricky Garard third (46:45). Toomey opened her title defense with the win over Aimee Cringle (50:16) and Lucy Campbell (51:36).

events.name: All Crossed Up
events.description:
For time:
20 wall walks
10 dumbbell shoulder-to-overheads
20 double-under crossovers
30 toes-to-bars
20 double-under crossovers
10 dumbbell shoulder-to-overheads
20 double-under crossovers
30 toes-to-bars
20 double-under crossovers
10 dumbbell shoulder-to-overheads

Single dumbbell: 100 lb men / 70 lb women (30 shoulder-to-overheads total).
Time cap: 10 minutes.
events.notes: First event inside MVP Arena. Garard out-touched defending event-style specialist Justin Medeiros by 0.35 seconds (6:06.46 to 6:06.81), with Jay Crouch third. Toomey won the women's race over Danielle Brandon (6:28.63) and Aimee Cringle (6:38.19). Double-under crossovers returned after debuting at the 2022 Games.

events.name: Climbing Couplet
events.description:
4-3-2-1 reps for time of:
Pegboard ascents
Squat clean + front squat (1 rep = 1 squat clean + 1 front squat)

Barbell load climbs each round:
Men: 235, 265, 285, 305 lb
Women: 145, 165, 185, 205 lb

Round 1 = 4 pegboard ascents + 4 complexes at the lightest bar, descending to 1 ascent + 1 complex at the heaviest. No published time cap.

loads.item: Squat clean + front squat (ascending per round)

events.notes: Eventual champion Jayson Hopper dominated the pegboard to take the win over Roman Khrennikov (5:38.67) and Harry Lightfoot (5:41.48). Fee Saghafi won the women's event by nearly a minute over Lydia Fish (9:30.58), with Siria Meha third (9:41.98).

events.name: Albany Grip Trip
events.description:
5 rounds for time of:
300-meter run
12 deadlifts (axle bar) - 350 lb men / 220 lb women
100-foot handstand walk

*150-foot handstand walk in the final round.
60 deadlifts and 550 feet of handstand walking total. No published time cap.
events.notes: The official workout card lists '12 deadlifts'; Morning Chalk Up/BarBend reported the bar as a grip-taxing axle, consistent with the event name. Some recaps printed the run as 400 meters, but the official card says 300 meters. Jay Crouch edged Kalyan Souza by under 4 seconds (16:32.62); Lucy Campbell took her first event win of the weekend over Haley Adams (17:01.34) and Toomey (17:37.63).

events.name: 1RM Back Squat
events.description:
Establish a 1-rep-max back squat.
Athletes lifted from racks on the arena floor and were given multiple attempts (winners took three rising attempts, e.g., Mertens went 525-555-570 lb); heaviest successful lift counts.
Score: load.
events.notes: First time the back squat was contested as a standalone event in Games history (previously only inside the CrossFit Total in 2007, 2018, and 2020). Colten Mertens' 570 lb broke the previous Games-best back squat of 540 lb that had stood for 18 years; Nick Mathew was second at 555 lb. Mirjam von Rohr won the women's event at 360 lb over Anikha Greer and Jennifer Muir (355 lb). Presented by LUXIAOJUN, with a $500 bonus for athletes lifting in the sponsor's shoes. Exact attempt/time-window rules were not published.

events.name: Throttle Up
events.description:
For time, wearing a weight vest:
35-calorie SkiErg
28 chest-to-bar pull-ups
24 burpee box jump-overs

Vest: 22 lb men / 16 lb women.
Box: 24 in men / 20 in women.
Time cap: 6 minutes.

First half of a back-to-back pair with Event 7 (Hammer Down), which started 7 minutes after this event.
events.notes: Presented by the United States Border Patrol. James Sprague won over Ricky Garard (3:14.21) and Calum Clements (3:17.41); Arielle Loewen took the women's sprint over Lucy McGonigle (3:55.56) and Toomey (3:56.12).

events.name: Hammer Down
events.description:
For time, starting 7 minutes after Event 6 (Throttle Up), no vest:
35-calorie Concept2 BikeErg
28 bar muscle-ups
24 burpee box jump-overs

Box: 24 in men / 20 in women.
Time cap: 8 minutes.
events.notes: Mirror image of Throttle Up: SkiErg swapped for BikeErg, chest-to-bars upgraded to bar muscle-ups, and the vest removed. Garard won over Colten Mertens (4:27.63) and Sprague (4:38.85). Lucy Campbell took her second event win of the day over Toomey (5:26.50) and Claudia Gluck (5:27.14).

events.name: Going Dark
events.description:
For time:
50-calorie (men) / 40-calorie (women) Echo bike
100-foot yoke carry
30 deficit handstand push-ups
100-foot yoke carry
50/40-calorie Echo bike

Yoke load and deficit depth were not published on the official workout card. No published time cap.
events.notes: The deficit handstand push-ups decided the race; many athletes overcooked the opening bike. Austin Hatfield's win vaulted him from 8th to 6th overall, ahead of Hopper (8:26.17) and Tudor Magda (8:27.34). Toomey won by over 40 seconds from Grace Walton (9:32.20) and Alexis Raptis (10:03.48).

events.name: Running Isabel
events.description:
5 rounds for time of:
200-foot run
6 snatches - 155 lb men / 105 lb women

30 snatches total (any style). A running twist on the benchmark Isabel (30 snatches for time), contested 20 lb / 10 lb heavier than the classic 135/95-lb loading. No published time cap.
events.notes: Hatfield went back-to-back on the final morning, beating Tudor Magda (2:36.02) with Dallin Pepper third. Jayson Hopper crossed just behind Hatfield but two no-reps dropped him to 11th, tightening the title race into the final event. Men's winning time widely reported as 2:35 flat (Fitness Volt lists 2:35.00).

events.name: Atlas
events.description:
For time:
9 thrusters, 3 rope climbs
15 thrusters, 5 rope climbs
21 thrusters, 7 rope climbs
Then: 100-foot overhead walking lunge

Barbell: 135 lb men / 95 lb women (thrusters and overhead lunge).
45 thrusters and 15 rope climbs total. No published time cap.
events.notes: Title-deciding finale with an ascending ladder (9/15/21 thrusters with 3/5/7 rope climbs) into a 100-foot overhead lunge to the finish. Justin Medeiros beat James Sprague by 0.48 seconds; Hopper tried to lunge unbroken, faltered in the final 10 feet, but still sealed his first title by 14 points. Garard finished one point ahead of Sprague for second in the closest men's podium race in Games history. Olivia Kerstetter's win (her second career individual event win) locked up third overall.

years.formatNotes: Format overhaul: 20 scored events for 30 men and 30 women across four competition days - July 22, 24, 25, and 26 - with no individual events on Thursday, July 23; the most events in a single Games in the sport's history. Day 1 (July 22) sent the field off-site for seven events at The Ranch in Aromas and the Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex, headlined by a reprised 2007 Hopper and the return of the CrossFit Total, whose three lifts (back squat, shoulder press, deadlift) are each scored as separate events worth a reduced points scale versus a standard event. Event 7 (Swim Standard), along with later events 9, 10, 16, and 17, stream exclusively on FloElite rather than the main CrossFit Games broadcast.
years.yearSummary: The 2026 Games are underway in San Jose, the arena days moving to SAP Center after two years in Fort Worth and Albany, with a record 20 scored events spread across four competition days and no individual events on the Thursday rest day. Day 1 sent both divisions off-site for seven events: a rerun of the inaugural 2007 Hopper, a 7,200-meter trail run at The Ranch, all three lifts of the CrossFit Total scored as separate events, a grass-oval bike race, and a pool swim/burpee event exclusive to FloElite. Jay Crouch, who won the reprised Hopper opener alongside his fiancee Madeline Sturt, held the men's overall lead wire-to-wire through six events before the closing pool swim flipped the top of the leaderboard. Aimee Cringle was the story of the women's field, winning three of the seven Day 1 events - the trail run, the CrossFit Total deadlift, and the bike race.

events.name: The 2007 Hopper
events.description:
For time:
1,000-meter row
5 rounds of:
25 pull-ups
7 push jerks

Push jerk: 135 lb men / 85 lb women. A rerun of The Hopper, the event that opened the inaugural 2007 CrossFit Games. Contested off-site on Day 1; exact site not officially specified. No published time cap.
events.notes: Crouch and Sturt are an engaged couple and both won the reprised opener. The original 2007 Hopper produced winning times of 13:07 (Marshall) for the men and 16:22 (Gentry) for the women; both 2026 winners nearly halved those times.

events.name: Ranch 7200
events.description:
For time:
7,200-meter trail run

Contested at The Ranch, Aromas, California. No published time cap.
events.notes: Garard, who won both parts of the 2024 Track and Field running event at Farrington Field outright, confirmed his standing as the field's premier runner; steep climbs at The Ranch forced some athletes to walk sections of the course.

events.name: The CrossFit Total - Back Squat
events.description:
Establish a 1-rep-max back squat, the first of three lifts in the reprised CrossFit Total (back squat, shoulder press, deadlift), each scored as its own event on a reduced points scale.

Score: load. No published time cap.

events.name: The CrossFit Total - Shoulder Press
events.description:
Establish a 1-rep-max strict shoulder press, the second of three lifts in the CrossFit Total.

Score: load. No published time cap.

events.name: The CrossFit Total - Deadlift
events.description:
Establish a 1-rep-max deadlift, the third and final lift of the CrossFit Total.

Score: load. No published time cap.
events.notes: Colten Mertens' 1,380 lb Total (555/260/565 lb) and Alex Gazan's 920 lb Total (330/170/420 lb) were reported by BoxRox as CrossFit Games CrossFit Total records; Patrick Vellner won the deadlift event at age 36.

events.name: Grass Oval Bicycle Race
events.description:
For time:
20 laps of a grass oval track

Contested at the Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex. Time cap: 25 minutes.
events.notes: The men's finish was a photo finish, the top five within 0.76 seconds of each other; Fiebig beat Pepper by 0.14 seconds. First Games cycling event since the 2023 Ride. Cringle's third event win of the day, after the trail run and the CrossFit Total deadlift.

events.name: Swim Standard
events.description:
For time:
200-meter swim
40 burpees
150-meter swim
30 burpees
100-meter swim
20 burpees
50-meter swim
10 burpees

25-meter pool presented by TYR, at the Morgan Hill Outdoor Complex. Time cap: 15 minutes.
events.notes: The first swim event at the Games since 2022's Rinse 'N' Repeat pool intervals, which Lucy Campbell also won; Morgan Hill also hosted the 2020 Games swim. Campbell, a former competitive swimmer, won by 69 seconds; Ty Jenkins' win was his first career individual event victory, at age 20. Streamed exclusively on FloElite.

events.name: Climbing Snail '26
events.description:
For time, wearing a weight vest (22 lb men / 16 lb women):
400-lb Snail push (100 feet men / 60 feet women)
Legless rope climbs (3 men / 2 women)
30 toes-to-bars
Rope climbs (5 men / 4 women)
Closing Snail push
10-minute time cap.
events.notes: First Snail at the Games since the 2016 Climbing Snail. Khrennikov won by nearly a minute for his sixth career event win, then gave his first victory interview delivered entirely in English. Alex Gazan won the women's event (4:55.22, on the women's course of shorter Snail pushes and fewer climbs) for her second event win of the 2026 Games.

events.name: 3D Throw
events.description:
For total distance, three sandbag throws (30 lb men / 20 lb women):
1 throw with the right foot forward
1 throw with the left foot forward
1 overhead backward throw
Distance measured from the back of the bag; throws landing outside the lane incur a 10-foot penalty. Scored as a 50-point event.
events.notes: First throw-for-distance test at the Games since the 2012 GHD Ball Toss. A 50-point event (the first 50-point events since 2016 per the broadcast, alongside the CrossFit Total). Malheiros won for his sixth career event win - one of his five priors was the 2022 Sandbag Ladder. Vellner and Dylan Hamming tied for second at 122 ft. James Sprague slipped on his final throw (16th), costing him the overall lead to Dallin Pepper. Abigail Domit won the women's event (108 ft) for her first career event win, ahead of Hannah Black (106 ft) and Alex Gazan (100 ft).

events.name: Run Hang Squat Clean
events.description:
4 rounds for time of:
660-meter run
10 hang squat cleans (225 lb men / 155 lb women, short barbell)
15-minute time cap.
events.notes: Runs exited the SAP Center onto an outdoor course. Crouch won by 13+ seconds for his second win of these Games (third career), with Medeiros edging Adler by 0.40s for second; Garard led early but a no-rep on his final round-three rep sank his event. Sprague finished 15:00.07 to Pepper 15:19.14, retaking the overall lead 614-607 - the second lead change of the day. Lawson won the women's event ahead of Campbell, who retook 2nd overall from Sturt (10th in the event) - that battle flipped three times on Friday.

events.name: Handstand Sprint
events.description:
For time: handstand walk course across the arena floor.
6-minute time cap.
events.notes: Name recalls the 2020 Handstand Sprint (Fraser/Wells). Victor Hoffer - who trained French artistic gymnastics from age three - won by nearly 25 seconds for his first career Games event win. Malheiros took his second podium of the day; New Zealand rookie Ben Fowler took his first career podium. After officials revised scoring, Sprague (14th in the event) retained the overall lead at 664 over Medeiros 648, Crouch 644 and Pepper 642 - a 22-point spread across the top four entering the hopper closer. Paige Rodgers won the women's event (1:56.58) for her first career event win; Danielle Brandon - winner of three straight handstand-family events 2021-2023 - finished outside the top ten. Rookie Lydia Fish took 3rd on an injured foot, part of an injured-ankle trio (Fish, Raptis, Greer) sweeping 3rd-5th. Lawson's 6th vaulted her from 5th to 2nd overall as Sturt fell to 5th - the women's podium picture reshuffled for the fourth time in the day.

events.name: The Hopper 2026
events.description:
Drawn live from the original 2007 hopper drum at Opening Ceremonies (snatch + toes-to-bar), structure set by fan vote:
3 rounds for time of:
21 toes-to-bars
7 unbroken power snatches
7 unbroken hang snatches
7 unbroken squat snatches
(95 lb men / 65 lb women)
6-minute time cap.
events.notes: The first hopper-drawn Games event since 2007, using the original drum. Unbroken snatch sets required (a dropped bar restarted the set). Mertens won for his third event win of the 2026 Games; Crouch 2nd, reigning champion Hopper 3rd, and Sprague 4th to retain the overall lead at the end of Day 2 (752 over Crouch 740, Medeiros 732, Pepper 718). Lucy Campbell won the women's event (5:02.48) for her sixth career event win - the workout was programmed by Tia-Clair Toomey and its structure chosen by fan vote. Cringle's finish-line buzzer initially failed to register; the official review credited her 4th (5:05), which moved Lawson to 5th on the event and decided 2nd overall: Campbell 739 edged Lawson 734, the fourth flip of second place in a single day. Cringle ended Day 2 at 826, an 87-point lead.

eras.name: The Ranch Era
eras.desc: Grassroots beginnings on a dirt hillside in Aromas, California. Handfuls of events, no qualification standard at first, athletes camping on site. The sport finding out what it was.

eras.name: The Carson Era
eras.desc: The Home Depot Center / StubHub Center years in Carson, California. The Games became a televised stadium sport: the Open (2011) and Regionals fed a professionalized field, sponsors arrived, and programming expanded into oceans, velodromes, and Camp Pendleton.

eras.name: The Madison Era
venues: The Ranch, with two Sunday finals events at the Morgan Hill Aquatics Center and Morgan Hill Sports Complex (Stage 1 contested online)
eras.desc: Seven years at the Alliant Energy Center in Madison, Wisconsin (with the 2020 pandemic final back at the Ranch). Deeper international fields, the cut era, and the Fraser and Toomey dynasties.

eras.name: The Touring Era
eras.desc: The Games leave Madison: Fort Worth in 2024, Albany in 2025. A transitional period for the sport - new ownership conversations, new formats, and a changing competitive landscape.

2007.pointsSystem: Placement-based points table taken directly from the official CrossFit Games leaderboard archive (games.crossfit.com / c3po API). Per event: 1st = 100, 2nd = 95, 3rd = 90, then a 1-point decrement per place from 4th onward (4th = 89, 5th = 88, ... i.e. 93 minus place for places >= 3). An athlete's totalPoints is the sum of points across the three events; James Fitzgerald won the men's title with 272 and Jolie Gentry the women's with 290. The exact 2007-era table was never formally published by CrossFit, so these point values are reproduced from the archived leaderboard rather than re-derived. Withdrawals (WD) scored 0 for the missed event (no withdrawn athlete reaches either top 10). Country of origin was not populated in the 2007 archive, so country is null for every athlete.

2008.pointsSystem: 2008 used cumulative-TIME scoring (lowest total elapsed time across all four events wins), not a points table - the format that gave the documentary its name 'Every Second Counts'. To fit the shared schema, each event's `points` is that athlete's event time expressed in whole seconds (from the official c3po leaderboard archive), and `totalPoints` is the athlete's cumulative time in seconds across all four events. LOWER IS BETTER. Event points sum exactly to totalPoints, and totalPoints in seconds equals the official overall finish time (e.g. Khalipa 236+157+238+166 = 797 s = 13:17; Matter 418+233+289+210 = 1150 s = 19:10).
sources: https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2008/leaderboards?division=1 (official leaderboard archive, men - per-athlete per-event time/seconds; scoreDisplay e.g. '3:56.0' = 236 s)

https://web.archive.org/web/20080920204637/http://games.crossfit.com/documents/CFGames08_Top5.pdf (official 'Top 5 in each event' PDF - used to correct the women's Hill Run places, which the c3po API deflates)

2009.pointsSystem: Placement-based (rank-sum) scoring: each athlete earned points equal to their finishing place in each event (1 point for 1st, 2 for 2nd, ...), and the lowest cumulative total won. This is not a 100-point table; points equal place for every event and totalPoints is the simple sum across the 8 events. Lower totalPoints = better. DNF/CUT athletes received heavy penalty points that dropped them below all complete finishers; none of those athletes are in either top 10 (e.g. Spencer Hendel and Annie Thorisdottir DNF'd the final chipper and finished 12th/11th, Cyndi Frieling DNF'd to 12th women).
sources: NOTE on country: the official archive API did not return per-athlete nationality (all 'Not specified'). Mikko Salo is well documented as Finland; the remainder of both top 10s came through US regional qualifiers in an overwhelmingly American 2009 field and are recorded as USA. Country is therefore high-confidence for Salo and the women's field and reasonable-but-inferred for the other men.

2010.pointsSystem: Placement-equals-points (no points table). Each athlete's finish position in an event equals the points earned for that event (1st = 1 point, 2nd = 2, etc.); totalPoints is the sum across all nine events and the lowest total wins. Ties shared the better place value (e.g., two athletes tied for 1st each scored 1, and the next athlete scored 3). totalPoints equals the official leaderboard overall score for each athlete; points equal the per-event rank exactly.
sources: Scoring is placement-equals-points; ranks and points are taken directly from the official c3po leaderboard archive and reconcile exactly to each athlete's overall score. Score displays are the official leaderboard values normalized ('rep' -> 'reps'). For the three-part Sunday final, leaderboard rep figures for athletes who FINISHED an event are encoded values (reps plus an unpublished time-remaining bonus), not literal reps, per the raw anchor file. For those events the place-1 winner's score uses the documented finishing time (Event 2010-07 men Froning 6:55; Event 2010-09 men Spealler 8:32; Event 2010-09 women Thorisdottir 7:34). Patrick Burke's Event 2010-09 finish (10:41) is documented and used; other finishers' encoded rep artifacts with no published time are set to null. Capped athletes' literal rep counts are kept as shown.

2011.pointsSystem: 2011 Reebok CrossFit Games 100-point scoring table. The event winner earned 100 points; points then dropped 5 per place through 6th (100, 95, 90, 85, 80, 75), 2 points per place from 7th through 30th (73, 71, 69, 67, 65, 63 ... 27), and 1 point per place beyond 30th (26, 25, 24, 23, 22 ...). Each of the 10 events paid out on this same scale, and final placing is the sum of event points; ties share a placing and its points (e.g. three men tied 2nd in The End 2 at 137 reps, each earning 95). Skills 1 (Event 2) and Skills 2 (Event 5) were scored internally by summing each athlete's rank across three component tests, then paid out on the standard scale, so their score column shows event points (e.g. '100 pt'), not a raw mark - the official leaderboard preserved only the final event placing for those two events.
sources: https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2011/leaderboards?division=1 (official CrossFit Games leaderboard archive API - per-athlete per-event rank, points, and score display for all men; primary source for every cell)
https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2011/leaderboards?division=2 (official leaderboard archive API for the women's division; primary source)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_CrossFit_Games (per-event results tables, final standings, and podium cross-check)

2012.pointsSystem: Two-tier relative placement scoring. Twelve events used a 100-point table (1st=100, 2nd=95, 3rd=90, 4th=85, 5th=80, then descending by smaller steps to 30th=27); three short tests (Broad Jump #2012-04, Ball Toss #2012-05, Sprint #2012-08) used a 50-point table (1st=50, 2nd=48, 3rd=46 ... 30th=17). Ties took the higher placement; time-capped events added 1 second per missing rep; max-effort events used 0.01 partial units per secondary-movement rep as tiebreaks. Final overall placing is the sum of event points.

2013.pointsSystem: Placement-points table (same as 2012), every event worth up to 100 points. 1st=100, 2nd=95, 3rd=90, 4th=85, 5th=80, 6th=75, then -2 per place from 6th-30th (7th=73 ... 30th=27), then -1 per place from 30th down (31st=26, 32nd=25, ...). Ties share the higher placement and equal points. Final standing is the sum of event points across all 12 events; the top 30 in each division after Event 10 advanced to Events 11-12.

2014.pointsSystem: Placement-based points from the official CrossFit Games leaderboard. Eleven events were worth up to 100 points and the two Sprint Sled races (events 2014-04 and 2014-05) were worth up to 50 points each. For the 100-point events points descend with finishing place per the 2014 table (1st=100, 2nd=95, 3rd=90, 4th=85, 5th=80, 6th=75, then dropping by 2 from 7th=73, 8th=71, 9th=69, 10th=67 ... through the field); the 50-point sled events use a halved version (1st=50, 2nd=48, 3rd=46, 7th=40 ...). Per-event place, score and points are taken directly from the official leaderboard archive; each athlete's 13 event point values sum to their overall total. The Clean Speed Ladder (2014-09) was scored by bracket placement, so its leaderboard score displays as '{rank} pt' rather than a time.

2015.pointsSystem: Each event scored on a graduated 100-point table for the winner: 1st=100, 2nd=94, 3rd=88, 4th=84, 5th=80, 6th=76, 7th=72, 8th=68, 9th=64, 10th=60, then descending by 2 (11th=58 ... 40th=0). Sprint Course 1 and Sprint Course 2 (2015-06, 2015-07) were worth 50 points to the winner on a halved table: 1st=50, 2nd=47, 3rd=44, 4th=42, 5th=40, 6th=38, 7th=36, 8th=34, 9th=32, 10th=30, 11th=29, then descending by 1 (40th=0). Total points are the sum across all 13 events; highest total wins. No athletes were cut during the Games. Tied places share that place's point value.

2016.pointsSystem: Per-event placement points on CrossFit's 2016 Games table for a 40-athlete field. Events 2016-01 through 2016-10, 2016-14 and 2016-15 awarded a maximum of 100 points to the event winner; the three short Sunday-morning tests - Handstand Walk (2016-11), Suicide Sprint (2016-12) and The Plow (2016-13) - were worth a maximum of 50 points each (half value). Points descend with place (full-value events: 1st=100, 2nd=94, 3rd=88, 4th=84, 5th=80, 6th=76, 7th=72, 8th=68, 9th=64, 10th=60, then ~2 per place; the three half-value events use roughly half those figures). Tied placings share points (e.g. Fraser and Ben Smith both 505 lb / 34 pts at place 23 in the deadlift ladder). Each athlete's 15 event points sum to totalPoints; the theoretical maximum is 1,350. All places, scores and points are taken from the official CrossFit Games leaderboard archive (c3po.crossfit.com).
2016.notes: Names use 2016 competition forms reconciled with the raw anchor: Kara Webb (later Kara Saunders), Anna Tunnicliffe (listed in the current archive as Anna Tobias), Katrin Davidsdottir and Sara Sigmundsdottir (Icelandic). Cole Sager's Event 2 (deadlift ladder) shows scoreDisplay '465 lb' but the lift was ruled invalid, so he placed 40th for 0 points. Events 11-13 (Sunday morning) are half-value (50-point) tests.

2017.pointsSystem: 2017 CrossFit Games graduated points table (40-place scale, max 100 per event). Points by finishing place: 1st 100, 2nd 94, 3rd 88, 4th 84, 5th 80, 6th 76, 7th 72, 8th 68, 9th 64, 10th 60, then descending by 2 per place: 11th 58, 12th 56, 13th 54, 14th 52, 15th 50, 16th 48, 17th 46, 18th 44, 19th 42, 20th 40, 21st 38, 22nd 36, 23rd 34, 24th 32, 25th 30, 26th 28, 27th 26, 28th 24, 29th 22, 30th 20, 31st 18, 32nd 16, 33rd 14, 34th 12, 35th 10, 36th 8, 37th 6, 38th 4, 39th 2, 40th 0. Every athlete contested all 13 events (no cuts). Ricky Garard originally finished 3rd overall but was disqualified after the Games for testolone/endurobol and banned four years; the official leaderboard archive still displays his event scores (including event wins in the Cyclocross and Madison Triplet) but marks his overall result DQ. He is therefore excluded from this top 10 and Patrick Vellner is elevated to 3rd, matching the corrected official standings.
sources: https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2017/leaderboards?division=1 (official CrossFit Games leaderboard archive API - per-event rank, points, and score display for all 39 men; primary source for every men's cell)

https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2017/leaderboards?division=2 (official CrossFit Games leaderboard archive API - per-event rank, points, and score display for all 40 women; primary source for every women's cell)
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_CrossFit_Games (results tables, final standings, and Ricky Garard DQ / Patrick Vellner elevation to 3rd; cross-check)

https://thebarbellspin.com/functional-fitness/tia-clair-toomey-edges-out-fellow-australian-kara-webb-for-fittest-on-earth-title/ (confirms Toomey edged Kara Webb by 2 points, 994 vs 992, the closest women's finish in Games history at the time)

Athlete naming follows the raw anchor file (e.g. 'Kara Webb' as competed in 2017, later Kara Saunders; 'Katrin Tanja Davidsdottir'; 'Tennil Reed-Beuerlein'; 'Sara Sigmundsdottir') so documented event winners resolve against the events data.

2018.pointsSystem: Standard CrossFit Games points table for a 40-athlete individual field: 1st = 100 points, descending by place (100, 94, 88, 84, 80, 76, 72, 68, 64, 60, then 58, 56, 54, 52, 50, 48, 46, 44, 42, 40, then -2 per place down to 38, 36, 34, 32, 30, 28, 26, 24, 22, 20, 18, 16, 14, 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 for places 21-39). 14 scored events; each athlete's final overall total is the sum of points across all 14 events. The Clean and Jerk Speed Ladder (event 6) was scored by elimination placement (leaderboard shows the place as '<n> pt').

2019.pointsSystem: Official CrossFit Games scaled points table (reintroduced 2019). Each event awards 100 points to the winner and descends by placement on a table whose step size widens as the field is cut. With the large opening field (Events 1-2) places fall by about 2 points each near the top (100, 98, 96, 94, ...); after the cut to 40/30 (Events 3-5) the step grows; the bracketed Sprint (Event 6, 20 athletes) falls by 5 per place (100, 95, 90, 85, ...); and for the final 10 (Events 7-12) points fall by 10 per place (100, 90, 80, 70, 60, 50, 40, 30, 20, 10). Tied athletes share the higher place and points. Final standing is the sum of event points (higher = better). Per-athlete places, scores, and points are taken directly from the official leaderboard archive API.
sources: https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2019/leaderboards?division=1 (men: per-athlete per-event rank, points, and scoreDisplay for the top 10; primary source)
https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2019/leaderboards?division=2 (women: per-athlete per-event rank, points, and scoreDisplay for the top 10; primary source)

https://fitnessvolt.com/2019-crossfit-games-results-final/ (final standings cross-check; note: FitnessVolt lists the disqualified Anna Fragkou at 9th and omits Brandon, whereas the official leaderboard excludes DQ athletes from the numbered standings - see notes)

NOTE: Anna Fragkou (Greece) finished inside the field on points (640) but was disqualified, so she carries no overall rank on the official leaderboard. With her removed, Þuríður Erla Helgadóttir is 9th and Danielle Brandon 10th. Brandon was cut after Event 6 (the progressive cut to 10) and did not contest Events 7-12; the official leaderboard shows those as CUT with 0 points. They are recorded here as place 11 (first athlete outside the final-10 cut), 0 points, null score. The four '0.0 lb' results in the Event 8 clean ladder (athletes who failed their opening bar and were separated by the 5-rep tiebreak) are recorded as null score with their real place and points.

2020.pointsSystem: Two-stage pandemic format with scores RESET between stages, so the official overall standing is decided by the FINALS only. Stage 1 (online, Sept 18-19): 30 athletes per division, 7 events scored on the standard 30-athlete Games table (100, 96, 92, 88, 84, 80, 76, 72, 68, 64, 60, 56, 52, 49, 46, 43, 40, 37, 34, 31, 28, 25, 22, 19, 16, 13, 10, 7, 4, 0 for places 1-30); only the top 5 per division advanced. Stage 2 finals (Oct 23-25, The Ranch): 5 athletes per division, 12 events scored 100-75-55-35-15 for places 1-5. totalPoints here is the official FINAL total = the sum of an athlete's finals event points (max 1200). To make per-athlete event points sum to that official total, the 7 Stage-1 events carry points:0 in this file (their points were reset and do NOT count toward the final standing); the real Stage-1 place and score are preserved for analysis. Overall ranks 1-5 are the five finalists ordered by finals points; ranks 6-10 are the next-best Stage-1 finishers, who were eliminated after Stage 1 (0 finals points). For ranks 6-10 the 12 finals events (2020-08..2020-19), which they did not contest, are recorded as place 6 (first position outside the 5-athlete final), score null, points 0.
sources: https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2020/leaderboards?division=1 (official CrossFit Games leaderboard API, men - per-event rank, points, scoreDisplay; primary source). Note: the API lists 20 'events' where ordinal 8 is a Stage-1 cumulative pseudo-event (score = sum of events 1-7 points); ordinals 1-7 map to raw 2020-01..2020-07 and ordinals 9-20 map to raw 2020-08..2020-19.
https://c3po.crossfit.com/api/leaderboards/v2/competitions/games/2020/leaderboards?division=2 (official CrossFit Games leaderboard API, women - same structure)

Reconciliation verified: Fraser finals total 1150 and Toomey 1025 match the API overall; men's margin 1150-605=545 and women's 1025-665=360 match the documented record finals margins. Every event's documented winner (raw file) places 1st where in the top 10.

2021.pointsSystem: Official CrossFit Games scaled points table (reintroduced 2019). Each event is worth 100 points to the winner; remaining places descend on a table whose step size scales to the number of athletes still competing. With the full field (Events 1-9) points fall by 3 per place from the top (100, 97, 94, 91, 88, 85, 82, 79, 76, 73, 70, ...). After the cut to 30 (Event 10) the spread widens (100, 96, 92, 88, 84, 80, ...), and after the cut to 20 (Events 11-15) points fall by 5 per place (100, 95, 90, 85, 80, 75, ...). Tied athletes share the higher place and its points. Final standing is the sum of event points (higher = better).

2022.pointsSystem: 2022 CrossFit Games individual scoring on a 100-point-per-event scale, using TWO tables because the field was cut once mid-competition (40->30 after Saturday's events, before the Sunday final day; this was the only mid-competition cut, per the official announcement games.crossfit.com/announcement/13704). Events 2022-01 through 2022-11 (40-athlete field) use the 40-athlete table: places 1-20 score 100, 97, 94, ... descending by 3 (1st=100, 5th=88, 10th=73, 15th=58, 20th=43); places 21-40 then descend by 2 (21st=40, 30th=22, 39th=4, 40th=2). Events 2022-12, 2022-13 and 2022-14 (Sunday, contested by the 30 remaining athletes) use the 30-athlete table: places 1-13 descend by 4 (1st=100, 2nd=96, 3rd=92, 4th=88, 5th=84, ... 13th=52), then places 14-30 descend by 3 (14th=49, 15th=46, ... 30th=1). First place is worth 100 on both tables. Thirteen named tests produced 14 scored events because Shuttle to Overhead was split into two 100-point scores (2A run time = event 2022-04, 2B max jerks = event 2022-05), so the maximum possible total was 1,400 points (a win in all 14 events). Final placement determined by total points across all 14 events. The Skill Speed Medley (2022-02) was a placement-only elimination race; the leaderboard records its score as the athlete's event rank (e.g. '1 pt').

2023.pointsSystem: Standard CrossFit Games points-per-place scaling table: 100 points for an event win, descending by finishing place. The table scales with field size, which shrank with the returning mid-competition cuts (40 athletes for Tests 1-6, 30 for Tests 7-9, 20 for Tests 10-12), so the points awarded for the same place differ across the three phases (e.g. 2nd place = 97 pts in a 40-athlete event but 96 pts in a 30-athlete event). Capped or last-place finishes can score 0. Maximum 1,200 points over 12 tests. Points shown are the official per-event awards from the CrossFit Games leaderboard archive.

2024.pointsSystem: Standard CrossFit Games points-per-place scale, max 100 for 1st in every event. Points descend with place on a table whose per-place increment depends on the field size for a given event: full-field Thursday/Friday/Saturday-morning events (~40, then ~32 after early withdrawals) step down by 3 per place from 100 (100, 97, 94, 91...), while the Sunday events contested by the top 30 use a compressed table stepping down by ~4 per place (100, 96, 92, 88...). Two events were scored on combined sub-event placement (2024-04 Track and Field, two separately timed parts) or elimination round-then-time (2024-06 Clean Ladder) rather than a single time. All place and points values are taken directly from the official CrossFit Games leaderboard archive (c3po API).
2024.notes: Scores for 2024-04 (Track and Field, combined placement of two separately timed parts) are null for all athletes: the leaderboard scores that event by combined rank, so no single time exists (the raw file records null winning scores and lists the fastest part times in its event notes). For 2024-06 (Clean Ladder, elimination rounds scored by round reached then time), the leaderboard score display is a placement; only the documented round-winning scores are recoverable, so place 1 carries the raw file's winning score and other athletes are null. All other events carry real leaderboard time/CAP scores.

2025.pointsSystem: 2025 CrossFit Games 100-point scoring table (30 athletes per division, 10 events, 1000 max): event winner earns 100 points, descending by placement as 100, 96, 92, 88, 84, 80, 76, 72, 68, 64, 60, 56, 52, 48, 45, 42, 39, 36, 33, 30, 27, 24, 21, 18, 15, 12, 9, 6, 3, 0 for places 1-30. Tied athletes receive the same placement and points (e.g., Austin Hatfield and Jack Rozema both placed 3rd in Event 5 at 515 lb, each earning 92 points).

assumptions: Reference body mass: men 195 lb (88.5 kg), women 145 lb (65.8 kg); identical within a division, so athlete comparisons inside an event depend only on time.
Lifts and gymnastics: external mechanical work (load and/or body mass x displacement) at 20% mechanical efficiency.
Running: 1.0 kcal per kg per km. Erg calories: displayed cal = kcal (the Concept2 calorie display is itself a metabolic estimate). Rowing: 70/60 J per m mechanical at 21% efficiency.
Loaded carries: load x distance x 0.04 horizontal-cost proxy. Yoke load (unpublished) estimated at 600/400 lb.
Event 5 (1RM Back Squat) is excluded from the power curve: no time component. Shown as peak strength.

The external-work method under-measures high-turnover gymnastics and jump-rope (double-under crossovers, fast toes-to-bars, wall walks) and grip/balance/isometric work. So "All Crossed Up" and "Climbing Couplet" read low in absolute watts despite being hard, fast efforts. That gap is a known limit of the model, not a fitness gap; those events are marked under-measured.
Capped scores (CAP+n): work scaled by completed fraction, time set to the estimated cap; flagged as estimates.
Erg devices (ski, bike, echo) use different internal calorie algorithms, so cross-device absolute comparisons are looser than within-event comparisons.
